These carry no FR id, so `capabilities().shipped` cannot announce them, and `capabilities()` does not list document keys: it is on every page's first load, and the keys a build reads are already published with it, as `@graview/core/document.schema.json` (JSON Schema, one per version). A host that writes a document for more than one build validates it against the schema of the oldest build it serves, or lets `readDocument` there refuse it by path.
- A picture or a document on a record arrived the same way (FR-162): the field types `image` and `file`, and `list` with `of: "image"` or `of: "file"`, in a document; `imageField()` and `fileField()` in a declaration, which `toDocument` writes as those types. The value is a `FileValue`, `{ href, name, type, bytes, width?, height?, caption? }`, its `href` a path on the host under its base (`/graview/files/3f9a….jpg`, or one relative to the page) and never a scheme, another host, a backslash or a path that climbs (`safeFileHref`); a store refuses any other value as it refuses any value that does not fit its field. A view's blocks gained `{ "image": "<field>", "as": "thumb" | "gallery", "label"? }`, judged by the check (`view-image`, an error about a block that could not be written before, and `view-format` for its `as`). `graview types` writes such a field as `FileValue` (or `readonly FileValue[]`). A build that predates them refuses the types and the block by path, so a host reads `capabilities().shipped` for FR-162 before it writes them. A compiled app carries the new field types within `graview-compiled@1`: a page that predates them cannot build such a field, refuses the compiled app as `compiled-shape` and compiles the document, which refuses the type by path. A change that leaves no record holding a file says so: `MigrationPlan.files` lists them, and the plan's words name them; what becomes of their bytes is the host's to decide.
- A link to another app arrived the same way (FR-171): the field type `app-link` in a document, `appLinkField()` in a declaration, which `toDocument` writes as that type. The value is another app's address — `@owner/app`, an id its host knows it by, or an absolute http(s) address, at most 500 characters (`isAppAddress`) — and a store refuses any other value as it refuses any value that does not fit its field. `graview types` writes it as `string`. A build that predates it refuses the type by path, so a host reads `capabilities().shipped` for FR-171 before it writes one; a compiled app carries it within `graview-compiled@1`, and a page that predates it refuses the compiled app as `compiled-shape` and compiles the document, which refuses the type by path. A relation whose `to` is another app's kind is the next line.
- A relation to a kind in another app arrived the same way (FR-171, the full relation): a relation's `to` may name `"@<app address>/<kind>"` — `"@nick/house/house"`, `"@app_kf5eydr9z58jzf/house"`, `"@https://example.com/a/house/house"` — every target one app's kind (`parseLinkedTarget`; the address is the one an app-link holds), and `linkedRecordField("@nick/house/house", { cardinality? })` in a declaration, which `toDocument` writes as that relation. The record that links keeps which far record as a value under the relation's name, `"<kind>:<id>"` (`linkedValue`), or a list of them for `"many"`; the far document is never written. `graview check` refuses a relation that mixes this app's kinds with another's (`linked-mixed`), reaches two apps (`linked-apps`), is no app's kind (`linked-target`), or says `inverse` (`linked-inverse`) or `appendOnly` (`linked-append-only`), a declared act that connects, severs or sets one (`act-linked`), and a rule that walks one with `out()` or `in()` (`rule-linked`); a page that compiles without the checker reads such a relation as no relation. The rule language walks it by name (`forHouse.listPrice`) through the reader of whoever is looking: a far record it cannot read, refused or not yet answered, reads as nothing and is said — a computed value's `refused` sentence, a rule `could-not-judge` where it would not hold without it — never thrown. `graview types` writes it as `string` (or `readonly string[]`). A build that predates it refuses an `@` target by path, so a host reads `capabilities().shipped` for FR-171 before it writes one; a compiled app carries it within `graview-compiled@1`.
- A phone, a place and a length of time arrived the same way, with no FR id (the Graview Roadmap's f-more-field-types): the field types `phone`, `place` and `duration` in a document, `phoneField()`, `placeField()` and `durationField()` in a declaration, which `toDocument` writes as those types. A phone is a string of at most 40 characters with at least three digits and only the spaces, `+`, `-`, `.`, `/`, parentheses and extension (`ext. 12`, `x12`) people write one with (`PHONE`); a place a string of at most 500; a duration a whole number of minutes, none less than none, which a duration field's `min`, `max` and `step` bound as a number's do (FR-114). A store refuses any other value as it refuses any value that does not fit its field. How each is said and linked is the page's and may change in a minor: a phone grouped as a reader in the US or Canada reads a North American number and as entered elsewhere, linked `tel:`; a place linked to maps.apple.com on Apple's platforms and Google's universal Maps address elsewhere, opened apart (`rel="noopener noreferrer"`); a duration said "1 h 30 min", and so is a computed field that says `as: "duration"` — which a TypeScript declaration says itself, and a document's compile writes for each computed field whose parsed expression adds, subtracts, negates or sums durations over a relation (`KindPlan.durations` in `graview-compiled@1`, optional; a face reads only `as`, never the expression's words). `graview types` writes a phone and a place as `string` and a duration as `number`. A build that predates them refuses the types by path; these carry no FR id, so a host validates a document that uses them against the `document.schema.json` of the oldest build it serves. A compiled app carries them within `graview-compiled@1`: a page that predates them cannot build such a field, refuses the compiled app as `compiled-shape` and compiles the document, which refuses the type by path.
- Markdown in a text field arrived the same way (FR-180): `"format": "markdown"` on a document's `text` field, `markdownField()` in a declaration (a string of at most 20,000 characters, marked so `isMarkdownField`, from `@graview/core/words`, says so through optional, default and nullable), which `toDocument` writes as that format. The value is kept as written. `retype-field` takes `"format": "markdown"` to make a text field Markdown and drops it when left out; `diffDocuments` says either change and neither is breaking. The checker refuses `markdown` on any type but `text`, and a number's format on a `text`, as `field-format`. A build that predates it refuses the format by path, so a host reads `capabilities().shipped` for FR-180 before it writes one; a compiled app carries it within `graview-compiled@1`. The record's page draws it as prose through `@graview/core/markdown` — headings demoted under the page's own, paragraphs with their line breaks kept, lists, emphasis, code, quotations, rules and tables, links only to `http:`, `https:` and `mailto:` (`rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`, a new tab), a picture as its words, and no HTML: within a major that reading only grows, and nothing it reads ever becomes markup. A row, a card, a describe line, a table cell, a search hit and a seat's line about a record say a text field by its start (`excerptOf`, from `@graview/core/words`): its first paragraph, heading or item, or about 160 characters, Markdown's syntax taken out; the exact words may be tuned within a major.
- A date that repeats arrived the same way, with no FR id (0.1.29, the Roadmap's f-recurring-dates): `"repeats": true` on a `date` or `datetime` field in a document, `repeatField()` beside the date in a declaration (`startsAtRepeat: repeatField()` beside `startsAt`), which `toDocument` writes as `repeats`. A record of the kind may keep, under the date's name and `Repeat`, `{ "every": "day" | "week" | "month" | "year", "interval"?: 1–99, "on"?: weekdays ("tue") for a week or days of the month (1–31, -1 the last) for a month, "until"?: a day, "count"?: 1–1000, "except"?: days, "continues"?: a record's id }`, or `null` once it no longer repeats; the date itself is the first occurrence, and a store refuses any other value (`validRepeat`). The key `<date>Repeat` is the framework's: a kind that has a field, relation or computed field of that name is refused (`repeat-clash`). Occurrences are worked out, never stored, and what reads the date reads the occurrence on or after the day it is judged on — the rule language, `today()`'s comparisons, a template, a list's sort, filter and date groups, and a kind's "in the next 7 days" — so a rule over a repeating date is judged anew when the day turns (FR-176) with nothing written. A day the series falls on that the month lacks (the 31st, Feb 29) is the month's last; a moment's time of day is kept as written, so one written without a zone stays at its wall time across a clock change and one written with a zone keeps that offset; `count` counts skipped days. Time zones beyond the one a moment says, and the rest of RFC 5545 (by-week-number, by-set-position, hourly), are not this. The edit vocabulary gained `set-repeats` (`{ kind, field, repeats }`, refused of a field that is not a date); `retype-field` away from a date lets `repeats` go; a migration moves a record's repeat with its date when the date is renamed, and a change that stops a date repeating drops each record's repeat and says so (`DocumentDiff` counts `<date>Repeat` among `removedFields`, so it is breaking). `graview types` writes `<date>Repeat?: Repeat | null`. A build that predates it refuses `repeats` as `unknown-key`, and a compiled app carries it within `graview-compiled@1`; a page that predates it refuses such a compiled app as `compiled-shape` and compiles the document, which refuses the key by path, so a host that writes `repeats` serves builds of 0.1.29 or later. These carry no FR id, so `capabilities().shipped` cannot announce them.
- What a declaration offers may grow without its text changing. An act that sets a status board's field to a value of its own (`book` setting `status` to `"booked"`) is a move to that value's column (FR-108), where a board offered only a free `set-<field>` act; where a named step reaches a column, the free act no longer does. A TypeScript mutation says the constants it sets as `sets`, optional, and one without it reads as before.
- Who the people are arrived the same way, with no FR id (the Graview Roadmap's f-people-kind, f-act-as-me, f-own-end-grants and "visibility scoped by relation"), each optional: `kinds.<kind>.people` (`true` on one kind: a record of it whose id is a principal's id is that person; the declaration's `people: true`, which the installation's `user` says), `policy.grants[].ownEnd` (`true`: every record the call names at the far end of the link the act connects or severs is the principal's own, and every link the act would make or break has the principal's own record at one end — so a connect on a relation of one that would replace somebody else's link is refused; a seat with no id of its own is never offered one) and `policy.sees[].via` (a relation: a record of the sight's kinds is seen only where that relation joins it, at either end, to the principal's own record; `own` reads every relation and what they made). `$me` in an act's effect is the acting person's own record of the people kind — the person, for an agent acting for one — and never an argument, so a document that used `$me` as an argument's name now means the acting person by it; an act that reaches `$me` for a principal with no such record is refused as `refused`, with a sentence. An op whose act wrote its author's own record where its call never named it — `$me`, or `ctx.me` in TypeScript — is undone only by that person (or their agent, or the system): anybody else is refused with a sentence, since the same call by them would have done something else. A document edit's `rename-relation` carries a sight's `via` with it, and `remove-relation` is refused while a sight reads the relation, as it is while a lens draws by it. A TypeScript act reads the same id as `ctx.me`. The checker's codes for them are `people-ambiguous`, `people-unsaid`, `sight-via-unknown-edge`, `sight-via-misses-people`, `grant-own-end-without-link` and a document's `act-me`; none fires on a declaration that says none of the new keys and no `$me`. A kind's JSON Schema says `"x-graview-people": true` on the people kind.
- The edit vocabulary gained the people and the policy (FR-170): `set-people` (`{ kind, people }`; `true` is refused as `people-ambiguous` while another kind is the people, so a move is `false` on the one, then `true` on the other), `add-grant` and `add-sight` (a grant or a sight as `policy.grants[]` and `policy.sees[]` hold one; a role the document's `roles` does not list joins it; a first sight on a document with no policy comes with a grant to everyone of every act, since a sight alone would take every act away), and `remove-grant` and `remove-sight` (named by what they say: a grant's `roles` and `mutations`, a sight's `roles` and `kinds`, each list in any order, and any other key given must match too; two that match are refused, asking for the key that tells them apart; a grant on no kind, `kinds: []`, gives nothing and is refused). `remove-kind` takes the kind's derived `edit-<kind>` and `remove-<kind>` out of every grant, and a grant left with no act or no kind goes; it is refused while every sight shows only that kind, since the sights gone would show everyone everything, so a change says `remove-sight` first. What the change leaves the people and the policy saying together is judged once it is whole, and refused at its last such edit by the checker's own codes (`people-unsaid`, `sight-via-unknown-edge`, `sight-via-misses-people`, `grant-own-end-without-link`); `grant-act` and `sight-kind` name an act or a kind the document lacks. `DocumentDiff`'s sentences say a grant, a sight, a role and the people kind in the words the edits say them, where a policy changed was "Who may do what changes." (still said of a change those do not cover). The studio says a grant, a sight and the people kind it changed as these ops, where a grant or a sight was a `studio-unsaid` finding and the people kind was not said at all. A build that predates them refuses the ops as an edit it does not know, so a host reads `capabilities().shipped` for FR-170 before it offers them.
- The rule language gained archived records (FR-173), optional within `graview-document@1`: `all('<kind>')` reads the live records as before, `all('<kind>', true)` the archived ones and `all('<kind>', 'all')` both, and `archived()` (or `archived(<record>)`) says whether a record is archived. An archived record is out of every computed field, fact, rule and count that does not ask for it, so a rule over a graph with none archived judges as before. A grant, a rule's repair and `editDocument`'s rename and removal of a kind read `archive-<kind>`, `unarchive-<kind>` and `merge-<kind>` as they read `edit-<kind>` and `remove-<kind>`, and `graview check` knows them, so a grant naming one is no longer `grant-unknown-mutation`.
- A kind that is never archived arrived the same way (FR-173): `kinds.<kind>.archives`, only ever `false`, says what `defineNode({ archives: false })` says — the kind is given its `edit-` and `remove-<kind>` and no `archive-`, `unarchive-` or `merge-<kind>` — and `toDocument` writes it. A document without it archives every kind as before. A grant naming one of the three on such a kind is `grant-act`, as a grant naming any act the app lacks is. The edit vocabulary gained `set-archives` (`{ kind, archives }`), which says what the app stops or starts offering and is refused as `grant-unknown-mutation` while a grant names one of the three. `planMigration` brings back, in the same op and said, a record already archived of a kind the change makes never archived (`counts.broughtBack`), and keeps `$archived` on every other record it plans, where it used to clear it.
- The app's locale says more than its money (FR-178), with no new key: `brand.locale` (a document's and a declaration's) is what every day, time and number is said in on every face, through `Intl` — a record's facts and glance, a template's `{due}` and `{due | date}`, a moment's `{at}`, a block's field, a rule's line, the calendar, the timeline's hours, the seat's lines, an arrangement's headings — and it is en-US where it names none: "Sep 10, 2023", "3:30 PM", "1,250", where every day was said day first before ("10 Sep 2023"). A host passes the reader's locale as `locale` on the embed, `GraviewProvider` and a pages `PageContext`, which wins over the brand's. What changes is the order and the punctuation of the words a person reads, never a stored value, an op, a tool schema or a finding code; `editDocument`'s and `diffDocuments`' sentences about a locale say "Days, times, numbers and money are written for …", and `describeApp` says what the locale makes of a day, a time and a figure. A host that matched the old day-first words reads them from its build's `capabilities().shipped`, FR-178.
- What a list offers to filter by arrived the same way, with no FR id (0.1.29, the Roadmap's f-filters-that-scale): `pages.lists`, `{ "<kind>": { "filters": [...] } }`, names in order what a kind's list offers — a field, a relation, `is`, or `<relation>.<field>` (a choice at the far end of a relation); a list a document does not name offers what it offered before. `arrange-pages` takes `filters: { "<kind>": [...] | null }` and refuses a key the kind cannot be filtered by, and a filter's grammar takes `<relation>.<field>:<value>`. A template's formatter `excerpt` (`{summary|excerpt}`, `{summary|excerpt: <20–1000>}`) arrived with it, the same way: a build that predates it refuses the template. The finding codes that came with them are warnings and judge only what is new: `pages-filter-unknown` (a filter the kind cannot be filtered by, passed over), `pages-kind-unknown`, the code it was, which now also says a kind `pages.lists` names that is not there and `view-whole-text` (a card or a row that puts a `text` field whole in a text block, which is clamped).
- The order and groups a kind's list opens in arrived the same way, with no FR id (0.1.30, asked while prioritizing the Graview Roadmap): `pages.lists.<kind>.sort` (`"<key>"` or `{ "by", "direction"?, "then"? }`, a field, a computed field or `label`) and `pages.lists.<kind>.group` (`"<field>"` or `{ "by", "order"?, "closed"? }`, a choice or yes-or-no field), beside `filters`; a list a document does not order or group opens as it did before. `arrange-pages` takes `sort: { "<kind>": … | null }` and `group: { "<kind>": … | null }`, which a build that predates them refuses as keys it does not know. Unlike `pages-filter-unknown`, the finding that came with them, `pages-list-arrangement`, is an error: a list sorted by what the kind does not have, grouped by a field that is not a choice or a yes or no, or ordering or closing a value that is not one of its choices is refused, since such a list would open some other way unsaid; only a document that says the new keys can meet it.
- How a number is said arrived with no new key (0.1.29, the money bug found on a Cloud app): a number field's `format` (`money`, `percent`) and `unit`, which a document always held, are now said on every face, and a number's `"format": "duration"` now means exactly the `duration` type — whole minutes, said, typed and described to a tool as that type is (`x-graview-type: "duration"`), its `unit` no longer read. The edit vocabulary gained `set-format` (`{ kind, field, format?, unit? }`, `null` clearing either): a number's `money`, `percent` or `duration` and `unit`, or a text field's `markdown` (FR-180), refused on a field the format does not fit, which a build that predates it refuses as an edit it does not know. `add-field` and `retype-field` refuse a format on a field it does not fit, which they took silently before for a number's format. One checker code, `field-format`, says a format on a field it does not fit in one sentence ("`"format": "money"` is a number's format, and this field is a text"): an error for `markdown`, a warning for a number's format, which a declaration could always hold; and a note for a number shown as a duration, which the type says once. `money-currency` warns of money with neither `brand.currency` nor a currency `unit`.
- No key is taken away from a document format within its version, and none is renamed without the old name still being read. 0.1.16 broke this: its American spelling pass renamed a setting's `honored` (was `honoured`) in the document as well as in the declaration, and its notes said the document format was unchanged, so every document `toDocument` wrote before 0.1.16 that carried settings failed to compile ("Nothing knows how to apply undefined"). Since 0.1.17 (FR-134), a key renamed within a format is a line in `RESPELLED` (`@graview/core/document`): every reader — `readDocument`, `compileDocument`, `appFrom` and `appFromOrCompile` on a compiled app an older build made, `diffDocuments` and `editDocument` — reads the old name as the new one, keeps the new one when a document says both, and never changes the document handed; `toDocument` and an edit write the new name. `respellDocument` does the same for a host and says which paths it respelled. A document stored with the old name is read the same on every later build of the major, so a host need not rewrite it, though its next save writes the new name. `packages/core/tests/document/fixtures/` keeps documents and compiled apps as older builds wrote them, made by those builds from npm, and each must compile; a test records every key path a document has been able to carry and fails when one is no longer read, by either name.
- What the app's own actor may tidy on its own (0.1.30) arrived the same way: `kinds.<kind>.tidying` (`"never"` or `"no-links"`) and `kinds.<kind>.edges.<relation>.tidying` (`"never"`), optional in `graview-document@1`, and the edit `set-tidying` (`{ kind, relation?, tidying: "never" | "no-links" | "allowed" }`), said in a sentence by `editDocument` and the same sentence by `diffDocuments`. A kind that says `"never"` is given no `leave-alone-<kind>` or `allow-tidying-<kind>`, and a grant naming one is the error `grant-act`; a relation that says what its kind already says is the warning `tidying-redundant`. A build that predates them refuses the keys as `unknown-key`.

#### 5. Derived tool names and input schemas

Tools are derived from the declaration (`createToolRuntime`, `graview mcp`), and a model that listed them before a change sends what it learned then.

- A change to a derived tool's name, description or input schema for an unchanged declaration is called out in a `Compatibility:` line, even when it is a fix.
- A change caused by the declaration (a renamed field renames an argument) is the app's change, not the framework's. The framework's part is saying which tools moved.
- FR-110 is such a change. Every derived `edit-<kind>` says `additionalProperties: false`, so an argument it does not take is refused as `invalid` where it was dropped. A document's act always says its `writes`, read off what its `sets` and effects set on its subject (`[]` when that is nothing), so an argument that only feeds a record the act makes no longer counts as a write of the subject, and `edit-<kind>` offers that field again. The conformance kit announces the two fixtures it moved (`document:vendors`, `document:two-lines`, 0.1.14). A TypeScript mutation that declares no `writes` is read as before.
- FR-121 is such a change. Every act's tool says `additionalProperties: false` — a document's act, a TypeScript mutation whose input is a plain `z.object`, `remove-<kind>` — and a call with an argument the act does not take is refused as `invalid`, naming what it takes, where the argument was dropped and the act ran without it. An act that creates still takes `id`. An input its author made `z.looseObject`, or gave a `catchall`, keeps what it is not told about and its tool says nothing new; one that is not an object's shape is not judged. An argument given as `undefined` is no argument. The conformance kit announces the two fixtures it moved (`document:vendors`, `document:two-lines`, 0.1.15).

- A file field's argument (FR-162) is described as an object of `href`, `name`, `type` and `bytes`, with `width`, `height` and `caption` optional, and a list of them as an array of that object; a seat may set one to a value the host's upload gave, and a value whose `href` is not a path on the host is refused as `invalid`. The derived `edit-<kind>` of a declaration that has no such field is unchanged.

- A number field's argument with a `format` or a `unit` (0.1.29) is described with `"x-graview-format"` (`money`, `percent`, `duration`, or `unit` for a measure), `"x-graview-currency"` for money and `"x-graview-unit"` for a measure or a duration, and a description saying the value is a plain number ("An amount of money in USD: a plain number, 1250.5 for 1,250.50 USD."; "A fraction said as a percent: 0.15 is 15%."), after the field's own description where it has one; the type and range are unchanged. The conformance kit announces it on `document:vendors`.

- An app-link field's argument (FR-171) is described as a string of at most 500 characters with the address's `pattern` and `"x-graview-app-link": true`; a seat sets it to another app's address, and anything else is refused as `invalid`. The derived `edit-<kind>` of a declaration that has no such field is unchanged.

- A relation to another app's kind (FR-171) is an argument of the derived `edit-<kind>`, described as a string of at most 300 characters — or an array of at most 200 — with `"x-graview-linked": { address, kinds, cardinality }` and a description saying it is `"<kind>:<id>"`; a seat finds the value with `find_linked` (`relation`, `query`, `of`, `limit`), a read listed only for an app with such a relation, answered through the host's `linkedRecords` as the seat. The tools of an app with no such relation are unchanged.

- A Markdown field's argument (FR-180) is described as the text field's string with `"contentMediaType": "text/markdown"` and its description ending "Written in Markdown."; what it takes is unchanged. A derived edit's history line says a string longer than 60 characters by its start (`excerpt`), not whole.

- A phone, a place and a duration field's argument says which with `"x-graview-type": "phone" | "place" | "duration"`, and a duration's `"x-graview-unit": "minutes"`; a field that says nothing of itself is described in words ("A length of time in whole minutes: 90 is 1 h 30 min."). A phone is a string with the phone's `pattern`, a place a string, a duration an `integer` of at least 0: a seat sends 90, never "1h 30m", which is refused as `invalid`. The derived `edit-<kind>` of a declaration that has none of these fields is unchanged.

- A date that repeats is described to a seat as an object of `every`, `interval`, `on`, `until`, `count`, `except` and `continues`, `additionalProperties: false`, with `"x-graview-repeat": true`, or `null`; the derived `edit-<kind>` of a kind with one takes it beside the date. Such a kind gains three derived acts, permitted as its edit is: `skip-<kind>` ("Skip this one", `{ id, on }`), `detach-<kind>` ("Change just this one", `{ id, on, …fields }`: a record of its own on that day, with the series' fields and the links the series makes, and the day an exception on the series) and `split-<kind>` ("Change from here", `{ id, on, …fields }`: the series ends the day before and a new one, `continues` naming it, starts that day); `field` names the date where a kind has more than one that repeats. Each refuses a day the series does not fall on as `refused`. A kind with no date that repeats gains none, and its tools are unchanged.

- Drawing a view and keeping it as a lens arrived as two tools a host opts into (the seat as a guide, B3): `draft_view`, a read, and `keep_lens`, which hands the host's `drafts.keep` the `add-lens` edit. A runtime lists them only when given `drafts` (`keep_lens` only with `drafts.keep`, and never on a read-only seat), and `toolDefinitions` only when told `drafts: "draw"` or `"keep"`, so a surface that did not ask keeps its tools and its hash. Their names, input schemas and answers are held to this section from now on. A lens either tool takes or returns is a declared lens (`{ title, lens, on, bindings?, options? }`) and is judged as one under the seat's sight; a kind the seat may not see is answered as one that is not there.

- FR-167 moved the read tools' answers and three input schemas. Every read answers at most `READ_CHARS` (8,000) characters of JSON, for a seat's turn and an MCP client alike. `get_graph` takes `offset` and answers a page of at most 25 records, the edges out of them, `total` and, when there are more, `more`; `get_node` takes `offset` and answers its links as `{ kind, id, label }`, 20 each way a page, where it answered whole edges; `get_violations` takes `offset` and answers `{ violations, total, more? }` where it answered an array; `search_graph` answers at most 20 hits whatever `limit` asked, with `more` and without `matched`. A field's text past 600 characters is cut and says its length, and any other read too long to fit answers `{ cut, partial }`. Within a host's turn, a call repeated with the same input is answered `{ already }`.

- FR-173 added three derived acts to every kind, beside `edit-<kind>` and `remove-<kind>`: `archive-<kind>` and `unarchive-<kind>` (`{ id }`, "Bring it back") and `merge-<kind>` (`{ id, into }`: the record `id` is archived and `into` takes its links). None is destructive; each is permitted through the acts that create the kind, as `remove-<kind>` is, and a grant may name each on its own. An app that declares an act of one of these names keeps its own. `search_graph` and `get_graph` take `archived` — `false` when unsaid, `true`, or `"all"` — and reach only the live records unless it is given; `get_node` reads an archived record by its id and says `archived: true`, as its links to one do. A seat that listed the tools before 0.1.29 sees three more per kind.
- A search's answer may now hold near hits (0.1.29, the Roadmap's f-semantic-search). When the words find fewer than `NEAR_BELOW` (5) records exactly, `search` (`@graview/core/search`) adds the records a near word finds — one slip in a word of 4–7 letters, two in a longer one, or another form of the word (a plural, -ing, -ed) — ranked after every exact hit, each a node hit with `near: true` and a `why` whose `strength` is `"near"`, with `asked` (the word typed), `matched` (the record's own word that answered) and `by` (`"spelling"`, `"stem"` or `"meaning"`). `near: false` asks for exact hits only, as going to a record by name and the conversation's "things called …" do. `search_graph` answers the same: a near hit says `near: true` and `why.matched`, so an agent never takes one for what it asked. A host's ranker (`HostAi.near`, or `near` on `createToolRuntime` and `createMcpHttpHandler`, or `rank` on `search`) is asked under the same rule with the candidates as `{ id, kind, label, texts }` and answers `{ id, score, matched? }[]` (0–1, nearer higher), at once or as a promise; the result carries it as `later`, which Find shows when it arrives and `search_graph` waits for. Find asks it only once the typing pauses (300 ms; an ask a later keystroke overtook answers nothing without reaching the host). Its `matched` is the host's words, not the record's: a hit keeps at most 80 characters of it (`MATCHED_MOST`), and `search_graph` hands it to an agent marked as words somebody else said, `{ untrusted: true, authoredBy: "the host's ranker", text }`, as it marks record text another seat wrote. **The ranker is handed only records the seat may see**: candidates are filtered by the seat's sight — the kinds kept from it and, record by record, the policy's `sees` — and by the kinds searched, the horizon and the conditions before it is asked, so a hidden record's text never reaches a host's model, and a score for an id it was not handed is dropped. A ranker that throws leaves the exact answer. Find's row for a near hit carries `data-near` and says "Near “<word>”" (`[data-testid="find-near"]`), with the field that answered; `/search`'s row says the same in `[data-testid="search-why"][data-near]`.
- The ninth walk (W-201) narrowed who a derived act reaches, and only where a grant to every role is the whole way to it. A kind's derived `edit-`, `remove-`, `archive-`, `unarchive-` and `merge-<kind>` ride the declared acts that make (or, for the edit, write) the kind; riding only a grant with `roles: "*"` that names those acts — "Anybody may join", `{ roles: "*", mutations: ["join"] }` — the derived act now reaches the records that seat made, as the log says who made each, and is refused on any other ("Not permitted: … — only on what you made; a coordinator can."), where it reached every record the seat could see. Nothing else changes: a grant of everything to everybody (`{ roles: "*", mutations: "*" }`, which `add-sight` writes on a document with no policy, FR-170) names every derived act outright and reaches every record a seat may see; a grant that names the derived act, or says `*`, reaches every record; and a role's own grant on the acts it rides (`{ roles: ["member"], mutations: ["join"] }`) reaches every record of the kind, as before. The tool list a seat is handed is unchanged; a call on another's record is refused as `forbidden`.

#### Not a surface: the look

The values the theme writes — the shipped palettes, the default faces, weights, radius and spacing, the kit's defaults — are not one of the five, and a patch may move them; the custom properties' names, the `Brand` keys and what each means are kept, and a change to a value is said on the changeset's `Compatibility:` line. A host that wants its look held still declares its own brand (`schemes`, `typography`, `shape`), which the framework never overrides.

The design kit's revision 03 is such a change. The shipped schemes are built on Graview's identity — paper `#f7f7f2`, ink `#18213a`, muted `#586174`, En Dash navy `#001769` as the light accent, `#9aabff` on a navy ground `#0a0f1f` in the dark — and paint no wash (`wash: "none"`); `TYPOGRAPHY.body` names Montserrat first (never fetched: the host loads it, or the system sans stands in), with three new properties for its weights (`--graview-weight-display`, `-body`, `-label`: 550, 450 and 600 on the framework's face, 600, 400 and 600 on a face a brand names); `h1` and `h2` are tracked at −0.025em; the default radius is 8 px (6 small) where it was 12 (9). A brand that names its own schemes, faces and radius draws exactly as before but for the heading weight (`--graview-weight-display`, 600 where the browser's bold was 700), the two largest headings' tracking and buttons' labels at 600. A brand derived with `brandFromAccent` over the shipped schemes takes the new grounds, panels and inks with its own accent. `system-sans` in a document is the system's own stack as it always was.

The routed face's type is the look too. It is one scale written by the theme as four custom properties — `--graview-text-small`, `--graview-text-body`, `--graview-text-heading` and `--graview-text-title` (0.833, 1, 1.2 and 1.728rem, a minor third from the reader's rem) — whose values a patch may move and whose names are kept; an app's own stylesheet that sets one moves that step wherever the face uses it. Headings take the theme's heading rule (`--graview-font-display`, `--graview-weight-display`), so a brand's own face and weight always win. What a host's page or harness reaches in a derived list is kept and said on the `Compatibility:` line when it moves: a row `li.graview-row` (in `ul.graview-rows`) holding its link `a.graview-row-title` and its glance `span.graview-row-glance`, a search hit the same row as `[data-testid="search-hit"]`, and a group's or a section's heading `h2.graview-group-head`. A row's glance leaves off the field its group is by and a choice the list is narrowed to one value of.

How the app bar lays itself out is the look too. Since it fits its box, it reads its own width and never the screen's (a phone's bar below 640 px of its own), Find is a small box that says its shortcut and is drawn wide while it is used, and the switch draws its icons alone when its words do not fit. What a host's page or harness reaches is kept as it was and said on the `Compatibility:` line when it moves: the test ids (`app-faces`, `app-face-scene`, `app-face-pages`, `app-find`, `app-find-open`, `find-box`, `nav-find`, `app-places-open`, `app-place-current`), the embed's `switch` option (`"words"`, the default, or `"icons"`), and the switch's `data-switch` (what was asked) and `data-switch-drawn` (what is drawn). A host that wants the switch held to its icons asks for `switch: "icons"`; nothing holds it to its words at every width, because a bar too narrow for them would run out of its box.

Where the places stand is the look as well (FR-145): on a bar with room after the name, the switch and the tools, the app's primary places stand on the row as words, in their order and never more than six with Home — the one the reader is on always among them — and the rest fold into "More"; with too little room the one control returns; a phone's bar keeps the one control. Which places are primary is the declaration's (`pages.primary`, kinds by name or plural and pictures by title); unsaid, every kind but the ones that support the others (a kind `pages.hide` leaves off the home, a kind of a module drawn only for its keepers, a note pointing at several kinds that nothing points at) stands, with its pictures, and Connections folds. On the scene the bar's places are the scene's (FR-144): "The whole thing" (`app-place-scene:whole`) and each picture (`app-place-scene:<kind>:<as>`), each with the scene's address for it as its `data-place-path` (`/places/overview` for the whole thing, the overview at altitude by its address alone since FR-154; `/places/overview#focus=…&in.view=<as>`). How many stand changes with the width, the brand's face and the app's places, so a harness never counts on it. What is kept, at every width and on both faces, is how a place is reached — one recipe:

1. Every place the bar offers is one element in the embed, `[data-testid="app-place-<key>"]`, carrying its `data-place-path` (the same key and path as before FR-145; a list's `kind:<kind>`, a picture's `place:<kind>:<as>`, the home's `home`, `connections`).
2. If that element is visible, press it (it stands on the row).
3. If not, press `[data-testid="app-places-open"]` — "More" where places stand, the one control where none do, on a phone the page's first line — and press it in `[data-testid="app-places"]`, the list it opens.
4. `[data-testid="app-place-current"]` says the place the reader is on: the one control's words, or the place standing on the row, marked `aria-current="page"`.

The list is grouped as before (`data-place-group`: `home`, `lists`, `pictures`), holding the places that do not stand; `app-places-open` is absent only when every place stands. The places standing on the row are inside `nav[data-testid="app-places-standing"]`.

How a list arranges is the look too: one quiet line under its title — the count in words ("16 tasks", "4 of 16 tasks" where something narrowed it), then "Sort", "Group" and "Filter", each opening a short list (`usePopover("arrange")`), and each condition as words with a ×; a narrow line is the count and one "Arrange". A list shorter than eight records has no controls unless its address arranged it. What a host's page or harness reaches is kept and said on the `Compatibility:` line when it moves: the line `[data-testid="<prefix>-bar"]` (`role="group"`, named "Arrange"; the prefix is `arrange` on the derived face and in a lens, `list` on an app's page that says so), the count `<prefix>-count` (with `<prefix>-kept` for "4 of 16"), the words `<prefix>-sort`, `<prefix>-group`, `<prefix>-add` (Filter) and `<prefix>-all` (Arrange) — buttons whose `value` is the chosen sort or group, as the selects' was — and the open list `[data-testid="arrange-list"]`, whose entries are buttons carrying the condition or choice as `data-value` (`due`, `holds:today`, `price:at-most:25000`) and `aria-pressed` for the one chosen; the direction's `<prefix>-direction-asc`/`-desc` and a date group's width `<prefix>-bucket-<day|week|month|year|decade>` are in those lists; a condition is `<prefix>-condition`; a date's day is asked in the list (`<prefix>-ask-day`, `<prefix>-day`, `<prefix>-day-add`). The addresses are as before (`?sort=`, `?group=`, `?filter=`, `?q=`, and the older `?by=`, `?<edge>=`, `?with=`, `?past=1`). Adding a record on a list page is one press, `[data-testid="act-open-<act>"]`, which opens `form-<act>` in place; the form stands open while the list is empty. A list of a kind with a `when` role (`fieldRoles.when`) opens, when its address says nothing, newest first by it at any length; a list of forty records or more otherwise opens by name; and a list of forty or more is sectioned by year or letter under `[data-testid="list-index"]` (each `list-section`); a harness that wants the stored order passes `?sort=`. An app's design that draws a list draws it with `ListPage` and so carries the same line and ids.

What a kind opens to in the scene when the app drew it no picture is the look too: going into its district (`#focus=aggregate:<kind>`, a kind with no lens) draws its stop in the box a lens fills — the plural, the count and the description; the creating act first, asked in place; what is overdue or due this week, its problems by rule and what changed since the reader last looked; then a picture its data chooses (a board by its main choice up to 300 records, a calendar where today's month has short records on its main date, else a table of its glance and relations, 50 rows at a time), with the other shape one press away and "Keep as a lens"; from altitude it opens in the panel beside the map a lens opens in (`lens-panel`), one panel at a time, focused as `#overview=1&focus=aggregate:<kind>`, where a single press still lists the district (`district-panel`), which is the seat's `add-lens` (`recipeDraft`, `@graview/tools/draft`). Which shape a kind gets may move with a patch. What a host's page or harness reaches is kept and said on the `Compatibility:` line when it moves: the region `[data-testid="kind-stop"]` (named by its `h2`, `data-graview-shape` `board`, `calendar` or `table`), `kind-stop-primary`, `kind-stop-acts`, `kind-stop-problems`, `kind-stop-as-<shape>` (`aria-pressed`), `kind-stop-keep`, the table `kind-stop-table`, each row a pick target for its record (`data-graview-pick`), with its `kind-stop-row-go` and `kind-stop-row-acts`, and `kind-stop-more`; the arranging line's prefix is `kind-arrange`; the table asked for is `in.as=table` in the stop. A view an app registers for the kind at many × full replaces the stop, as before.

What a page draws while a part it fetches has not arrived is kept the same way (FR-139): the line `[data-testid="lazy-part-missing"]` in the part's place, a polite status, with its button `[data-testid="lazy-part-retry"]` ("Try again"); a part that never arrives draws that line and throws nothing into the embed. `retryingImport` is on its own entry, `@graview/core/retry`, for a page only: the main entry, tools and ship carry no `import()` of a computed URL, which workerd refuses. A selected record in the scene marks its host `data-graview-record-focus`, under a declared page is one `[data-graview-primitive="panel"]` holding `[data-graview-spec="page"]`, and a district's name is `[data-graview-district-name]` (FR-141, FR-143). In an embed, the panes the bar opens and the notices at the foot stay inside the embed's box where they fit there; a harness finds them there, never at the window's foot.

How the quick ask looks is the look too (Roadmap f-quick-ask-framework; no face draws a field at its foot or a conversation thread): ⌘K (Ctrl+K) opens one card beside what the reader is on, a command bar that becomes the answer card when words are asked, and Find's `/` stays Find's. What a host's page or harness reaches is kept and said on the `Compatibility:` line when it moves: the marker `[data-graview-quick-ask]` (`scene` or `pages`) where it is drawn; the card `[data-testid="quick-ask"]` (`role="region"`, named "Ask about <the thing>" or "Answer about <the thing>", `data-quick-ask` `bar` or `answer`, `data-quick-ask-beside` the `data-graview-view` it stands beside or `page`, `data-quick-ask-side` `right`, `left`, `below`, `above` or `top`), its line `quick-ask-about`, its field `quick-ask-input` (a combobox), each row `quick-ask-option` (`data-quick-ask-kind` `act`, `show`, `place`, `record` or `ask`), `quick-ask-close`; on an answer, `quick-answer`, `quick-answer-asked`, `quick-answer-text`, each `quick-answer-offer` (`data-ai-offer`, `data-ai-offer-type`), and the ghost of the changes it proposed, `ai-ghost`, drawn on the card; the context menu's `[data-menu-item="ai-ask"]` ("Ask about this…"); Find's last row `find-ask` and the search page's `search-ask`; the lines' key beside Up, `lines-key` and its pane `lines-key-pane`. The Shell's, a routed face's and the embed's `quickAsk` (a boolean; a setting kept from 0.1.30 as `"field"` or `"hidden"` is read with `quickAskOf`) and `handle.setQuickAsk` say whether it is drawn, and it is drawn only where the host's `ai` gives a model and is not `off`. Nothing in it asks a reader which machine answers: the host gives it once, as `ai` (`HostAi`: `answer`, `thinking`, `fast`, and the `complete`, `turn` and `decide` behind them); its answers are kept as AI interactions (`ask.kind` `"ask"`, with `answer`), and a change it proposed is a ghost accepted as one batch through `ai:<interaction>`. The conversation (`useGraview().seatTalk`, kept under `graview:seat:<the app's name>`) is the engine a product's own `ChatPanel` draws; no face draws it.

Sentences a program may match are said in the changeset when they move: the insight observation `insight:load:<id>:<edge>` reads "<name> <the relation's words>: all <n> <plural>" (or "<n> of the <m> <plural>") since FR-142, a relation's words from its `description` or `inverse`, else its key spoken (`edgeWords`, `@graview/core/words`).

- Every kind is given `leave-alone-<kind>` and `allow-tidying-<kind>` (`{ id }`, 0.1.30), unless its declaration says it is never tidied, and an agent's tools gain `list_suggestions`, `accept_suggestion` and `decline_suggestion` (`{ suggestion }`). The conformance kit announces the new tools on `document:vendors`, `document:two-lines` and `document:shortlist-0.1.10`.

### The conformance kit

`@graview/core/conformance` ships fixtures: declaration documents with the check findings and tool schemas this framework made of them, and op logs with the snapshot hash each folds to. `conformance()` runs them against this build, or against a build a host hands it, and returns the differences by fixture id. A host runs it before it takes a version.

The fixtures are append-only. `node scripts/conformance-fixtures.mjs` only ever adds a fixture with a new id, and a lock holds the rest. A change to a recorded fixture is an announced difference (`ANNOUNCED`), with the version that made it and what changed.

### The Compatibility line

A pull request that touches a file on one of the five surfaces asks every changeset it adds for a line:

```md
Compatibility: additive — `Operation.via` is a new optional field; ops without it read as before.
```

The line says the surface, whether the change is *additive*, *breaking* or *unchanged*, and for whom. `scripts/require-changeset.mjs` refuses a changeset without one (CI's `changeset` job), and the files that count as each surface are in `scripts/lib/surfaces.mjs`. The line goes into each package's CHANGELOG with the rest of the changeset, so every release lists what it did to compatibility.

### `capabilities()`

```ts
import { capabilities } from "@graview/core";

capabilities();
// { version: "0.1.22", protocol: 1, documentFormats: ["graview-document@1"], formats: { snapshot: 1, op: 1 },
//   shipped: ["FR-06", "FR-11", …] }
```

`shipped` lists the ids of the seams this build ships, by the ids Graview Cloud filed them under. A host retires its interim for a seam when the id appears. A test holds the list to the FR ids the changesets name, so a seam cannot ship unannounced or be announced without shipping.

`FRAMEWORK_VERSION` is the version alone, for a host that records which framework folded a store.

---

What a Graview version may change on the five surfaces a host holds it to — ops, stored formats, the wire, the declaration and the tool names — and how a host reads what a build ships.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/stability.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/releases.html

## 0.1.33

Published October 17, 2026 · the current version

A read-only calendar takes its own changes under a policy, and a host keeps Notify me in its own store.

- **A read-only connection works under a policy.** A calendar the app only reads now brings its own changes in when the app declares who may do what, and a change the app refuses is reported as refused rather than as the calendar being unreachable.
- **Notify me on a hosted page.** `mount` takes the host's subscription store, so subscriptions made from the right-click or a record page are kept by the host on both faces; keeping them that way adds no parser to the first load, about 9.4 KB less than before.

**Before you upgrade:** `SyncReport.refused` may now name an inbound change (`SyncRefusal`, with the remote `resource` and `id`), and `offline` is true only when the remote itself fails. `mount` and `<Embed>` take `subscriptions`.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.33) · [The full changelog for 0.1.33](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0133)

## 0.1.32

Published October 17, 2026

Ask with ⌘K and the right-click, be told when things happen, a faster first load, the GPU by default, and a Google calendar kept in step.

- **The AI where you are working.** ⌘K opens a bar beside what you're on that completes its acts, places and records; anything else is asked, and the answer is a card beside the record or list. The right-click offers suggestions, fills, new records and panels, picked only from what you may see and do. Every proposed change is previewed first, accepted all or some, and undone in one step, and Activity keeps each AI interaction.
- **Notify me.** Subscribe to an act, a kind or a record in two presses from a right-click, a record page or chat. A change by someone else that you may see tells the host once.
- **Faster.** First load to interactive is 31–38% faster on a desk and on a slowed phone, held by a CI budget, and the scene draws on the GPU where the browser can, with unfocused planes blurred.
- **Dates and calendars.** One date and date-time editor everywhere that reads "tomorrow 3pm" or "Fri 10:30" and shows times in your zone. A Google calendar can be declared in the app (a calendar, a color or #tag filter, read-only or both ways) and kept in step by `graview serve`, proven against Google itself.
- Twelve controls covered by another were fixed, and graview.dev shows the inline AI and gains this page.
- **Fewer presses to add a record.** A list's Add button now stands beside its heading, so making a record from the keyboard on the pages takes 10–14 presses where it took 17–22.
- **The GPU only where clicks land.** A Chrome whose capture build would hit-test where a view was laid out rather than where it was drawn now draws on the DOM path, so a press, a screen reader and a focused field always meet what is on screen.
- **Signs, panels and embeds that stay out of the way.** A sign at the map's edge steps past a district's name, "Go to it" hands the keyboard straight on to the record it went to, a lens is drawn in the room it has from its first frame, and an embedded app draws nothing over its host page.

**Also in it: 0.1.31**, which was versioned and never published, so its changes shipped here. Ask with ⌘K and the right-click, be told when things happen, a faster first load, the GPU by default, and a Google calendar kept in step. The quick ask and the right-click AI, notify me, a faster first load, the GPU by default, one date editor and a Google calendar kept in step, all described under 0.1.32.

**Before you upgrade:** The old seat's input, its panel and their settings are removed, along with the routed face's own copy: `quickAsk` replaces their setting on the Shell, the pages and the embed, and `quickAskOf` reads a stored one. The full list of removed names is in the changelog. The Shell's and the embed's `renderer` defaults to `auto`. A document's `datetime` is asked for with the date editor. The hosted page carries about 3.5 KB more up front (1.3 KB gzipped).

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.32) · [The full changelog for 0.1.32](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0132)

## 0.1.30

Published October 15, 2026

Play an app back, link across apps, an actor that tidies, and graview.dev as a Graview app.

- **Playback.** Open the app as it stood at any moment, and restore it to there.
- **Linked records.** A relation can point at a kind in another app, read there as whoever is looking.
- **An actor that tidies.** The app's own actor suggests fixes, which a person accepts or declines.
- A first look for a new app, an emoji as the app's mark, kind lists you can sort and group, navigation with filters and sections, a right-click menu on Pages and images by URL.
- Eighteen author requests and a run of scene and lens bugs fixed, a screen-reader pass, and the GPU path past 128 live views. graview.dev itself is now a Graview app.

**Before you upgrade:** `Store.at` and `Store.seqAt` are replaced by `pastOf` and `seqAt` on the new `@graview/core/past`. A role that removed, archived or merged other people's records only through the act that makes the kind now needs those acts named in its grant.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.30) · [The full changelog for 0.1.30](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0130)

## 0.1.29

Published October 14, 2026

A large release of field types, list tools and data features, on a lighter page.

- **New field types:** links to another app, Markdown text, phone, place and duration, and money, percent and unit formats; dates and numbers said the US way.
- **Records:** archive and merge records, lineage and provisional links, repeating dates, field-level sight, acting on several records at once, and `importRows` for bringing data in.
- **Lists:** fuzzy search, filters that scale to large lists, and cards you can read at a glance.
- `renderPlace` writes a place as static HTML, guest views can show pictures, and `store.tick` reports what changed.
- The map is laid out along the ground, and the hosted page is lighter up front than 0.1.28 despite everything added.

**Before you upgrade:** Breaking for imports: `edgeWords` and `valueWords` move to `@graview/core/words`, and the address helpers (`withShown`, `withQuery` and the rest) move out of `@graview/layout`; nothing is aliased. The scene's map is laid out anew, so a `sceneThumbnail` draws a different picture. Ops, stored formats, the wire and tool schemas are unchanged.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.29) · [The full changelog for 0.1.29](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0129)

## 0.1.28

Published October 13, 2026

The people kind, grants and sights are named edits.

`editDocument` gains `set-people`, `add-grant`, `remove-grant`, `add-sight` and `remove-sight`, so who may do and see what can be changed as a named, previewed edit instead of a raw patch. Each is previewed in words and refused with the checker's own codes.

**Before you upgrade:** Ops, stored formats, the wire, the document format and check codes are unchanged. The edit vocabulary gains five ops, and an edit's refusal can now carry a specific code where every refusal was `edit`.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.28) · [The full changelog for 0.1.28](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0128)

## 0.1.27

Published October 12, 2026

People in a document, bounded seat reads, and links that say why they did not go.

- A document can name the kind that stands for its people, and its acts can say `$me` for the person acting.
- A grant can hold to your own end of a link, and a sight can reach the records that link to you.
- A seat's reads are bounded, and a worker view's link or navigate says why it did not go.

**Before you upgrade:** Breaking: `answerSeenBy` moved to its own entry, the read tools' answer shapes changed, `useSeatConversation` requires `said`, and `$me` is reserved as an argument name.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.27) · [The full changelog for 0.1.27](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0127)

## 0.1.26

Published October 12, 2026

Pictures and files on records, and a failed AI turn says why.

A kind can carry pictures and documents: `imageField()`, `fileField()`, the image block, and uploads through the host's files seam. When a host's AI turn fails, the seat shows the host's own explanation.

**Before you upgrade:** Breaking for imports only: the form helpers (`formFields` and its neighbors) moved to their own entry. Ops, stored formats, the wire, the document format and tool schemas are unchanged.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.26) · [The full changelog for 0.1.26](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0126)

## 0.1.25

Published October 12, 2026

The app on a phone: the seat closes and the screen fills.

On a phone, the open seat is put away by its close button, a tap on its grab line or a pull down, and the keyboard goes with it. An app fills the phone after it rotates.

**Before you upgrade:** Tool schemas move to `@graview/core/json-schema`.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.25) · [The full changelog for 0.1.25](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0125)

## 0.1.24

Published October 12, 2026

Every seat judged over what it sees, problems that open on their fix, and a fit on the smallest phone.

- What a seat is told is worked out over what that seat can see.
- Pressing a problem opens its repairs, wherever the record sits, and a record is renamed by pressing its name.
- The bar and the home's counts fit a 320-pixel phone at the largest text size.
- Names, yes-or-no fields and facts read in plain words. Also sync fixes.

**Before you upgrade:** Ops, stored formats, the wire, the declaration, check codes and tool schemas are unchanged; only where some types are declared moved.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.24) · [The full changelog for 0.1.24](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0124)

## 0.1.23

Published October 11, 2026

The seat's turn, without the weight.

`turnThroughMessages` has its own entry, `@graview/tools/turn`, under 2 KB, so a host can wire the seat's turn up front without loading the whole tools package on first paint.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.23) · [The full changelog for 0.1.23](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0123)

## 0.1.22

Published October 11, 2026

Preview and doctor, typed documents, and a seat that reads before it answers.

- `graview preview` serves a document and a seed with Graview's own faces over them, no product needed, and `graview shots` photographs places headless.
- `graview doctor` says whether a product is on one Graview release.
- Documents are typed from the editor to the face, can declare facts about the whole graph, and give kinds a natural time and author field. Declared blocks have stable keys.
- The seat reads records with tools before it answers, the sync engine resolves conflicts as it is told, and kinds with no records fold into More.
- A security and correctness review of 0.1.21.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.22) · [The full changelog for 0.1.22](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0122)

## 0.1.21

Published October 11, 2026

Who's here on every bar, axe-clean markup, and a way back in the scene.

- Who else is here shows on the bar on both faces and on a phone.
- The framework's own markup passes axe-core for WCAG 2.0 to 2.2 A and AA, at desktop and phone widths, light and dark.
- The scene gets its own way back, and the overview has an address that survives a server round trip.
- A broken rule states its values to a host that reads only its message, and a read-only role is no longer warned for doing nothing.

**Before you upgrade:** Ops, stored formats, the wire, the document and compiled formats, check codes and tool schemas are unchanged; some presence and test-id behavior a harness reads moved.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.21) · [The full changelog for 0.1.21](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0121)

## 0.1.20

Published October 10, 2026

List pages lead with their records, and rules read like sentences.

- A list page puts its records first instead of a tall header of title and related links.
- A rule written in the rule language says its shape in plain words.
- An agent opening a new product finds what to read at the root.
- Fixed: a connect that replaces now replaces the right link, one mistake gives one check finding, and the scene from an empty address lands where the scene opens.

**Before you upgrade:** Additive: the document format gains an optional `pages.primary`, and check gains two warnings about it. Which places stand on the bar changed.

[The release on GitHub](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/releases/tag/graview%400.1.20) · [The full changelog for 0.1.20](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md#0120)

## 0.1.19

Published October 9, 2026

The seat floats, takes you where you ask, and draws views you can keep.

- The seat is no longer a rail down the scene's edge: it floats, quietly, on both faces.
- Ask it to go somewhere and it goes, matching the request against what the declaration and the graph already name, without a model.
- Ask it for a way of seeing and it drafts a view that can be kept as a lens. Who-and-when questions are answered from the graph with no model.
- The host chooses the AI once, instead of the reader picking from a menu. The whole-page shell wears the one app bar, and the hosted page carries 9.5 KB less before the app draws.

**Before you upgrade:** Breaking for the components and API a host's seat reaches: the `Companion` family is removed for the floating seat and `HostAi`. Ops, stored formats, the wire, the document format and tool schemas are unchanged.

## 0.1.2

Published October 3, 2026

The declaration as a document, a live wire, and guest views.

- **The declaration is a document:** one JSON object that compiles into the same app `defineApp` declares, with an edit vocabulary of twenty-one operations, rules written as expressions, and templates as data.
- **A live wire:** `openRemote({ live: true })` pushes every op to every browser as it lands, MCP is served over HTTP, and logs can be folded and compacted.
- **Guest views:** `@graview/guest`, a view somebody else wrote, in a sandboxed frame that can only ask.
- A SQL adapter, stored formats that carry their version, a conformance kit, and `docs/stability.md`, the promise a version keeps.

**Also in it: 0.1.1**, which was versioned and never published, so its changes shipped here. A record read whole, in its own words. **Before you upgrade:** Breaking: a store served without `seatOf` answers 401 until it passes `trustSeatHeaders: true`, `graview serve` binds 127.0.0.1, a host's `seatOf` receives a web `Request`, a full palette needs the `good` and `bad` tokens, and a kind no sight names is seen only by the system.

Published October 2, 2026

The first public release of the framework on npm.

Graview's first release to npm: a framework where a typed context graph is the interface rather than the backing store. One declaration per kind drives the layout, the legal actions, the agent tools and the accessibility labels. `graview` is the tool and `@graview/*` the framework, all at one version, under the Elastic License 2.0.

# Documentation

This is the documentation for Graview, a TypeScript framework that derives an app’s interface, permissions and agent tools from one declaration. Everything here except the concepts is written out of the repository, so none of it can disagree with the code it describes.

```sh
npm create graview@latest my-app
```

New here? [Getting started](https://graview.dev/docs/getting-started.html) is the first hour; [the garden, grown](https://graview.dev/progression.html) is the whole framework in sixteen live steps.

- [Getting started](https://graview.dev/docs/getting-started.html): One command to a running product, what it writes, and the loop from there.

- [The tour](https://graview.dev/tour.html): Every surface Graview derives from one declaration, each beside a live frame.
- [Concepts](https://graview.dev/docs/concepts.html): The declaration, and the seven things in it.
- [Working with a model](https://graview.dev/docs/agents.html): The seat, the typed tools, what a model reads, and the studio.
- [Live demos](https://graview.dev/docs/demos.html): Every surface of the garden, running on the page, and the example apps.
- [Packages (14)](https://graview.dev/docs/packages.html): What each ships and what each exports.
- [Skills (19)](https://graview.dev/docs/skills.html): What your assistant reads before it writes.
- [The CLI](https://graview.dev/docs/cli.html): create, check, types, docs, describe, lens, figure, serve, skills.
- [What check says (105)](https://graview.dev/docs/checks.html): Every finding, and how loudly.
- [Stability](https://graview.dev/docs/stability.html): What a version may change, and what a host can hold it to.

- [The garden, grown](https://graview.dev/progression.html): Sixteen live chapters, from one kind to a product.
- [This site, as an app](https://graview.dev/docs/site.html): graview.dev is a Graview app: its pages are records, and its city is one click away.

# The packages

Graview, a TypeScript framework that derives an app’s interface, permissions and agent tools from one declaration, ships as 14 npm packages at one version. `graview` is the tool a person installs; `@graview/*` is the framework a product imports, each package depending only on the ones beneath it.

## All of them

- [@graview/core](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/core.html): The graph, the log, the schema and the checker. Everything a Graview app declares, and the CLI that verifies it.
- [create-graview](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/create-graview.html): Start a product on Graview: `npm create graview my-app`. The conventional door to `graview create`.
- [@graview/embed](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/embed.html): Mount a declared Graview app into any element — the scene, the Graview, or the routed pages — without the Shell, sized and themed within the element.
- [graview](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/graview.html): The Graview command line: start a product, check its declaration, write its agent docs, serve its store, preview a document with no product and photograph its places, say whether a product is on one release, host it for an agent over MCP, apply an act to it, sync its seed, install the authoring skills. The tool; @graview/* is the framework.
- [@graview/guest](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/guest.html): Guest views: somebody else's React or plain script in a sandboxed frame, or a hardened classic worker drawing a component kit, shown only what the viewer may see, able only to ask for acts the viewer's seat then applies.
- [@graview/layout](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/layout.html): Where every node goes: three planes, one pure function of the graph and the view state.
- [@graview/pages](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/pages.html): The traditional face: a routed webapp derived from the same declaration that drives the scene.
- [@graview/primitives](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/primitives.html): The primitive set, the lenses, the workbench and the visual system.
- [@graview/react](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/react.html): The React binding: a provider, a scene, and the hooks an app builds on.
- [@graview/render](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/render.html): The spatial renderer: the GPU capture path where the browser can capture into WebGPU, the DOM path everywhere else, one picture and one accessibility tree on both.
- [@graview/ship](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/ship.html): What every deployment needs, hosted or self-hosted: persistence wiring, op-log-native migrations, export, health.
- [@graview/skills](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/skills.html): Skills that teach an assistant the authoring moves, each ending in a real graview check verdict.
- [@graview/studio](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/studio.html): The declaration itself as a graph: kinds, fields, edges, acts, rules, roles and grants as nodes, edited with ordinary mutations in Graview's own interface, checked before they are applied, migrated, and written back as the files graview create writes.
- [@graview/tools](https://graview.dev/docs/packages/tools.html): Derived affordances and the agent tool surface, generated from the same declarations; graview mcp and graview apply host it against a real store.

---

The 14 packages Graview ships, what each is for, and what each exports.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/packages.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt
