The acts: `add-kind`, `rename-kind`, `remove-kind`, `add-field`, `rename-field`, `remove-field`, `retype-field`, `set-required`, `set-options`, `describe-field` (a field changed in place: `{ id: "field:vendor.notes", type: "string" }`), `add-edge`, `remove-edge`, `add-act`, `remove-act`, `add-rule`, `remove-rule`, `name-repair`, `forget-repair`, `add-role`, `grant`, `revoke-grant`, and the derived `edit-<kind>` for what no act names (an inverse, a title, a lifecycle).

1. **Check before you apply.** `studio.check()` is `graview check` on the declaration as it now stands. `studio.apply()` refuses while there are errors and says which; otherwise it hands back `{ app, migration }` — the migration is `null` when a stored graph needs nothing, else a `{ from, to, title, apply }` to append to the app's migrations (the new app already carries it and the bumped version).

**Opened on a document** (`createStudio(compileDocument(d).app)`, with `compileDocument` from `@graview/core/check`), the studio hands back a document, not TypeScript. `studio.edits()` is the change as `editDocument`'s own ops (`add-field`, `rename-field`, `set-required`, `set-options`, `add-relation`, `remove-act`, `add-rule`, and a grant, a sight or the people kind as `add-grant`, `remove-grant`, `add-sight`, `remove-sight` and `set-people` …); `studio.document()` is the opened document with them applied, every act, label, brand and money field untouched. `check()`, `would()` and `apply()` judge by compiling that document, and `apply()` hands back `document` with `app` compiled from it. A copied app, or one with its policy swapped, says it: `createStudio(app, { document })`; without one, `whyNoDocument()` says why. A change no op says yet — a relation's cardinality, a lifecycle, a role, retyping a money field — comes back as `documentFindings`, one sentence each, and no document. Ask ahead what it keeps but will not change: `uneditable(document)` is one note per format, unit or list item type (`kinds.vendor.fields.quote`).

Without the studio, `editDocument` covers the rest of a document too: `add-lens` (`replace` retitles; `at` puts one back), `remove-lens`, `{ op: "set-lens-hidden" }` (`hidden: true` keeps a lens off the bar and the page list, still reached by its address, a link or `navigate`), `set-home`, `arrange-pages` (`order`, `hide`, `first`, `scene` and `pages` — the switch's words; `null` clears), `set-computed` (`expr: null` removes it and what reads it), `set-format` (a number's `format` — `money`, `percent`, `duration` — and `unit`, or a text field's `markdown`; `null` clears; said in words, "money in USD — 10000 reads $10,000"), and `set-view` for a kind's slot, `slot: "home"`, or `lens: "<title>"`. Blocks are checked as they are set. A rename reaches lenses, the home, pages and computed expressions through the parser; removing a field or relation a lens draws by is refused, naming the lens. Computed fields are studio nodes, kept on hand-back and written-back TypeScript.

1. **Write it back.** `studio.files({ schemaVar: "gardenSchema" })` is `src/domain/schema.ts`, `mutations.ts`, `invariants.ts` and, with roles, `policy.ts` — the files `graview create` writes. Shape is what a graph carries: an act the studio declared gets a body from what it says (create, connect, sever, write); an act the checkout wrote keeps the checkout's body under the studio's declaration; a rule the studio declared judges nothing until the checkout gives it an `evaluate`. Read the files before you commit them, and keep a hand-written body where the comment says so.

1. **Let an agent propose.** `studio.propose(call, agentPrincipal, intent)` applies under the agent's seat in a batch of its own; `studio.proposals()` lists what stands; `studio.decline(batchId)` undoes one; accepting is applying. In the interface, the trail shows the agent's turn with its undo, like any turn.

1. **Put it on a page.** The studio is an app: mount `studioApp()` with `declarationToGraph(app)` as the seed, and register `createStudioLens(app).View` over `kind` with a title — a place, "What the checker says", one press from anywhere.

### Then find out whether it worked

Run `graview check` on the app the studio applied, and the checkout's own verify on the files it wrote. Say what they said.

### What the check cannot see

- Whether a body the studio wrote does what the person meant. It does what the act declares — create, connect, sever, write — and nothing more.
- Whether a rule the studio declared is right. It judges nothing until the checkout gives it an `evaluate`; the checker sees a rule, not a judgment.
- Whether a migration is safe for data it has not met. It is computed against the stored graph when it runs; look at the primitives on a copy.
- Whether the files should replace the checkout's. Read them; a hand-written body is the checkout's to keep.

---

Open an app's declaration as a graph in Graview's own interface, change it with ordinary acts, let graview check judge the result before it is applied, migrate a stored graph, and write the declaration back as the files graview create writes.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-studio.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-view-drawing.html

# graview-view-drawing

`graview-view-drawing` is one of Graview's 19 authoring skills: instructions an AI coding assistant such as Claude Code or Codex reads before it changes a Graview app. What it teaches: Draw in a Graview worker view — the HTML, SVG and CSS the host keeps of it, the app's tokens and brand, and the images a view may show (the app's logo, the app's own images, the pictures on records) — and find out what the host refused rather than assuming it drew.

Installed into a project by `graview skills install .`, and read by whichever assistant is working beside you.

## The skill

## Drawing in a worker view

A worker view (`graview-worker-view`: its manifest, its global, its writes and its limits) draws by saying markup; the host draws what the open kit keeps of it into a shadow root it owns, and lists the rest. **What it may draw is broad; what it may load is only what the host chose.** Every image it shows is one the host holds, made for it, or lists the origin of.

### What it may draw

HTML's sectioning, headings, text, lists, tables, `details`/`summary`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `label`, `fieldset`, `meter`, `progress` and `img`. SVG's `svg`, `g`, shapes, `path`, `text`, gradients, `clipPath`, `mask`, `marker`, `pattern`, `symbol` and `use href="#id"`. Attributes: `id`, `class`, `style`, `title`, `role`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, and each element's own. CSS for layout, grid, flex, color, type, transitions, `@keyframes`, `@media`, `@supports` and `@container`.

Never drawn: `script`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, `link`, `meta`, `base`, `style`, `form`, `video`, `canvas`, SVG `image` and `foreignObject`; any `href`, `srcset` or `on*` attribute; `src` on anything but `img`, and on `img` any address but the ones below. In CSS: `url()` except `url(#id)` on `fill`, `stroke`, `clip-path` or `marker`; `@import`; `@font-face`; `image-set()`, `attr()` and other unlisted functions; `position: fixed`; `:host`. `position: sticky` is kept — a header held in place sticks within the view, whose region is painted contained — and `all` takes its keywords (`button.toggle { all: unset }` takes the browser's chrome off a toggle). What the host leaves out it lists in `refused`; `graview.refused` is the runtime's own early word on the last render.

A view never speaks as the app's chrome. `nav`, `header`, `footer`, `aside` and `search` are drawn as `div`, and `output` as `span`, each with what it holds. They lose their landmark or status role, and a selector for them in your stylesheet still matches. A `section` is never named (no `aria-label` or `title`), so it stays out of the landmarks. `role` takes no landmark or notice's role (`navigation`, `region`, `status`, `alert`, …).

### The app's look

**Draw with the app's tokens**, so light and dark follow the app's own toggle: `var(--graview-panel)`, `--graview-ground`, `--graview-ink`, `--graview-ink-muted`, `--graview-edge`, `--graview-accent`, `--graview-font-body`, `--graview-font-display` (headings, as the app's), `--graview-font-mono`, `--graview-radius`. Presentation attributes do not take `var()`; put paints in the stylesheet (`.bar { fill: var(--graview-accent) }`). For what the view computes, `props.theme` says the same tokens as values, with `scheme`, the app's `name` and its `logo`. A brand change or the app's toggle pushes `theme` again.

### The images a view may show

An `img`'s `src` is drawn only when it is one of these; any other address — another site, a path of the app's of your own making — is refused, and said once in the view's console and the host's problems, with the address:

- **A `data:` image** the view holds: PNG, GIF, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, BMP or SVG. Keep it small; it is part of the view's source.
- **The app's logo**: `<img src="${props.theme.logo}">`. The host made it from the brand's mark (a `blob:` URL of the page, or a `data:` image where the page's policy refuses `blob:`). Absent when the brand has none.
- **An image the app holds**, by the content address it was stored at: `/graview/assets/<sha256>.<ext>` (what Graview Cloud's `add_image` answers). It is drawn only where the host says where those live — the `asset` resolver on the view's definition — and refused elsewhere.
- **An `https:` image on an origin the host lists** — `images: { origins: ["https://upload.wikimedia.org"] }` on the view's definition (and on a headless run). The view never chooses an origin: an address is data it can write, so an open list would let it send what it reads anywhere. It is asked for with no referrer. Unlisted, a URL on a record is refused.
- **A picture on a record.** Say `pictures: true` in the manifest, or `{ width: 400 }`, the widest the view draws one in CSS pixels. Each file on a record the view is handed is then `{ name, type, bytes, width, height, caption, src, left }` in its field, never the host's path to it. `src` is the address the host made from the bytes, fetched as the reader and made smaller to `width`; it is absent on the first push, and a push follows when it is ready. `left` says why a picture will never come: past one picture's byte budget or the view's, or not loaded. A document, and an SVG, has no `src`: show its name, type and size.

```js
const photos = (job.photos || []).map((photo) => photo.src
  ? graview.html`<img data-key="${photo.name}" src="${photo.src}" alt="${photo.caption || photo.name}">`
  : graview.html`<p data-key="${photo.name}">${photo.left || photo.name}</p>`);
```

Without `pictures`, a record's file comes as the record keeps it: its `href` draws only where it is the app's own image (`/graview/assets/…`).

**Keep a picture in an `image` field**, which holds the uploaded file (what `add_image` stores), never its bytes as words: a `data:` URI in a text field is cut at 20,000 characters, and in the view's source it counts against its size.

### Then find out whether it worked

1. `graview check` the app, and `checkManifest(manifest, store)` from `@graview/guest/host/views`: it says what is wrong with `pictures`.
2. `graview view check view.js --app <app> --manifest manifest.json --seed <seed.json> --roles <role>` says what it drew. Headless, a picture comes without `src`, so draw its name until it does.
3. Open the place and read the view's `refused` (`WorkerView.refused`, or `graview.refused` in its console): every element, attribute and address the host left out, and why.
4. Toggle the app to dark, and change the brand where you can. Does the view follow, logo and all?
5. As a member who may see fewer records, are the pictures on the records they may not see absent — not merely hidden?

### What the check cannot see

`graview check` judges the declaration, and `refused` judges the markup; neither sees whether the drawing reads. A picture drawn at full width on a phone, an image with no `alt`, a token used for a meaning it does not carry, a chart whose colors fail in dark: only looking at it on both faces, at 390 and on a desk, in both schemes, sees that.

---

Draw in a Graview worker view — the HTML, SVG and CSS the host keeps of it, the app's tokens and brand, and the images a view may show (the app's logo, the app's own images, the pictures on records) — and find out what the host refused rather than assuming it drew.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-view-drawing.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-worker-view.html

# graview-worker-view

`graview-worker-view` is one of Graview's 19 authoring skills: instructions an AI coding assistant such as Claude Code or Codex reads before it changes a Graview app. What it teaches: Write a Graview worker view — one plain script, no imports and no build, that draws HTML, SVG and CSS for a kind or the home through the graview global — with a manifest the host enforces, and prove it runs rather than assuming it does.

Installed into a project by `graview skills install .`, and read by whichever assistant is working beside you.

## The skill

## A worker view

A worker view is for what the declared blocks cannot draw: a chart, a grid of cards, a front page with a figure and a ring. It is one plain script. The host runs it in a hardened worker with no network, no storage and no DOM of its own, and draws what it says into a shadow root inside a region the host owns. **What it may draw is broad; what it may reach is not.** Write it against one global, `graview`. There is nothing to import and nothing to build; the word `import` may not appear in it at all, even in a comment, and nor may `export`.

### The manifest

Every view comes with a manifest the host enforces:

```js
{ name: "packages", title: "The packages", attach: "package", cardinality: "many",
  reads: { kinds: ["offer"], edges: ["includes"] },
  acts: ["set-summary", { act: "set-standing", as: "recommend", constants: { standing: "recommended" } }] }
```

- `name` is lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. Acts are recorded `via: "view:<name>"`.
- `title` makes it a named place on both faces, with the slug `placeSlug(title)` (`"the-packages"`).
- `attach` is a kind, or `"home"` for the front page's body (cardinality `many`).
- `reads` lists the other kinds and the edges it is shown. Nothing else is handed to it.
- `acts` lists the acts it may ask for, by name. An entry with `as` and `constants` is another name for the same act with arguments the view cannot change.
- A view of one record (`cardinality: "one"`) is drawn above the record's own fields, which stay editable. `replaces: "page"` draws it alone instead; only then is the record changed through the view alone.
- `pictures: true` (or `{ width }`) hands each file on a record with an address the host made from its bytes, never its path: `graview-view-drawing` says how a view shows it.

A manifest that names a kind, an edge or an act the app does not declare is refused before the view starts.

### The global

```js
graview.style(css)              // the view's one stylesheet
graview.onProps((props) => …)   // every push of what it is shown (and at once)
graview.props                   // the last push
graview.render(markup)          // draw: a string, graview.html`…`, or nodes
graview.html`<li>${x}</li>`     // markup; every value put in is escaped
graview.on("click", ".card", (event) => …)   // also input, change, keydown, toggle
graview.act(name, args)         // ask for an act: resolves { ok, intent } or { ok: false, reason, message }
graview.navigate("offer:7")     // a record, else a place or a kind's list by slug
graview.navigate({ place: "features", where: { stage: "building" }, section: "Shipping soon" })
```

`props` holds `node`, the record a view of one is drawn for, and `nodes`, the records a view of many is drawn for and those it reads. A record is plain data: its `id`, `kind` and `label`, and each field on it by name, so a deliverable's draft is `props.node.draft`; there is no `fields` key. A view of one finds its record in `node`, never in `nodes`. Then `edges` (`{ kind, from, to }` among them), `label` (its title), `acts` (`{ name, title }`, those the viewer may run), `places` (`{ as, title }`), and `theme` (`scheme`, `accent`, `panel`, `ink`, `fontDisplay`, `radius` …, the app's `name`, and its `logo` as a URL the host made). `render` keeps what it can, by element and by `data-key` or `id`, so give repeated rows a `data-key`: a field being typed in keeps its text across a push. An event carries `value`, `checked`, `key`, `pressed` for a bound press, and `element`, what the selector matched: read its `data-*`. Elements lack `closest`, `matches` and `dataset`.

```js
graview.on("click", "[data-go]", (e) => graview.navigate(e.element.getAttribute("data-go")));
```

### What it may draw

HTML, SVG and one stylesheet, drawn with the app's `--graview-*` tokens so light and dark follow the app's toggle; nothing that loads or escapes. What the host keeps, the tokens, and the only images a view may show (the app's logo, the app's own images, the pictures on records) are `graview-view-drawing`. What the host leaves out it lists in `refused`.

### Links

`<a data-record="offer:7">` and `<a data-place="the-packages">` are links the host follows, on both faces. `<a href="https://…">` is drawn as text. A destination is a record's id, else a place by its slug or its title (`data-place="songs-by-writer"` or `"Songs by writer"`), else a kind's list (`features` or `feature`); any other says why, naming the places.

A list or a lens may be gone to **narrowed**: `where: { stage: "building" }` in navigate, `data-filter="stage:building"` on a link — the words the list's own arranging line writes, so the address is `/features?filter= stage%3Abuilding` and can be shared. A lens narrows the records it is handed; a blocks lens lists what its own `where` says. Any destination may take a **section**, a heading's words or an element's id (`section: "Every feature"`, `data-section`): the page scrolls there and gives it the keyboard (`#every-feature`). On the scene a list is the kind's stop narrowed (`in.filter`); a section is looked for there too. A filter on a field the kind lacks, or a choice it lacks, goes nowhere and says why (`Features have no field "stag" to filter by; they filter by …`), so link to the list narrowed rather than to a lens per filter; a lens kept only as a link target can be hidden (set-lens-hidden, `graview-pages`).

### Writes

An act must be in the manifest. If every member of the app sees every record, `graview.act` applies it as given. Otherwise **only a press applies an act**: a person's click on an element with `data-act`. Its arguments come only from the record it is bound to (`data-record`, on it or around it), the manifest's constants, and the fields in its `fieldset`, named for the act's arguments and typed by the person:

```html
<fieldset>
  <input name="summary" placeholder="What it is">
  <button data-act="set-summary" data-record="package:start">Say it</button>
</fieldset>
```

A field the view filled (`value="…"`) is the view's until the person empties it, and a press carrying it is refused. To offer a record's own text to edit, let the host fill it: `data-prefill` names the field, and `name` is the same.

```html
<fieldset data-record="deliverable:email">
  <textarea name="draft" data-prefill="draft"></textarea>
  <button data-act="set-draft">Save the draft</button>
</fieldset>
```

The host fills it with the record's whole value, line breaks kept, when an act in the fieldset writes that field of that record and the person may run it there; otherwise it stays empty. The person edits it in place, and it goes only back into that field. A view may empty a field after a press. A radio or a select is the person's pick, not their words: its value goes only if it is one the act declares (an enum's option) or a record the view was shown. The press is applied before the view hears it; read `event.pressed`.

### Limits

About 256 kB of source, 5 000 drawn nodes, 120 messages a second, 1 000 ms per push, and 100 ms a second of the page's time drawing it. Past any of them the view is stopped and the plain face of its records is drawn instead, with why. Draw summaries, not every row of a huge set. Work a view schedules with timers between pushes is not timed per push. It may keep its worker busy just under the heartbeat's 5 s; the page stays responsive, the person's CPU does not: never spin.

### Worked examples

`examples/offers-list.js` is a list lens: rows linking to their records, and a note typed and pressed in. `examples/front-page.js` is a home: a headline, a figure, an SVG ring and cards linking to a place. `examples/a-record.js` is a view of one record: a deliverable's subject and its draft as paragraphs, read off `props.node`, and "Edit draft" with the draft prefilled. Each opens with its manifest.

### Registering it

```ts
import { registerWorkerView, workerHome } from "@graview/guest/host/views";
views: (schema, registry) => registerWorkerView(registry, { manifest, worker: { source } }),
pages.surface("home", workerHome({ manifest: front, worker: { source: frontSource } }));
```

A view with `attach: "home"` given to `registerWorkerView` is the home's own view: the routed home's body, the page the app opens on — full width under the bar on a desk too — and the app's declared home is drawn if it fails.

### Then find out whether it worked

1. `graview check` the app the view names: a manifest is only as sound as the declaration it reads. `checkManifest(manifest, store)` and `checkViewSource(source)` from `@graview/guest/host/views` must both say nothing.
2. Run it headless, with no network, as a member who may see less than you, over a seed: `graview view check view.js --app <app> --manifest manifest.json --seed <seed.json> --roles <role>`. It prints what the view drew, said as `graview describe` says a place, or why it will not do: `error` (what it threw), `nodes`, `flood`, `slow`, `act` (an act its manifest does not name), `manifest` or `source`. Run it on an empty seed too. In code, `runWorkerViewHeadless` from `@graview/guest/headless` does the same in an isolate you supply.
3. Open the place on both faces as that member. Is anything shown that they should not see? Does the region carry no `data-worker-view-failed`? `start` there means the view never ran: a page with a Content-Security-Policy needs `worker-src blob:` and `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, and the note under the plain face names what it lacks.
4. Toggle the app to dark. Does the view restyle?
5. Press each bound button with typed words, then again with a field the view filled. The first applies and the second is refused. A prefilled field is filled only for a seat that may write it.

### What the check cannot see

`graview check` judges the declaration, not the script. It cannot see a view that throws on an empty graph, draws the wrong number, or takes too long on a big one. Only running it does: `graview view check` on an empty app, a full one, and a member with narrow sight. A headless run is one push with timers that never fire, and nothing laid out, so it cannot see an animation or a layout that breaks at 390; the faces can. Nor can it see a view that misleads. The host keeps it from reaching or leaking anything, not from arranging what the person may see badly.

---

Write a Graview worker view — one plain script, no imports and no build, that draws HTML, SVG and CSS for a kind or the home through the graview global — with a manifest the host enforces, and prove it runs rather than assuming it does.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-worker-view.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/recipes.html

# Recipes

A recipe is one prompt to hand your agent, with a different task each, and the app an agent made of it. Each was made from the prompt alone in Larkspur, a made-up repository, and each runs on its page.

```sh
Read https://graview.dev/start.md, then turn this repo's docs into a Graview app.
```

## The recipes

- [Your docs, as an app](https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/docs.html): The repository's docs, the modules they cover and who owns each, with every module that has no doc or no owner flagged and the repair offered.
- [Your decisions, as an app](https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/decisions.html): The architecture decision records: what each decided, what it superseded and which modules it affects, with the loose ends flagged.
- [Your dependencies, as an upgrade plan](https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/dependencies.html): Every third-party package, the version pinned against the latest on npm, the modules that use it and the upgrade it needs, with the risky ones flagged.

---

Graview recipes: one prompt to hand an agent, with a different task each, and the app it made, checked on every push and live on its page.

# Your decisions, as an app

This recipe is what an agent made of one prompt, in a repository it had never seen. The architecture decision records: what each decided, what it superseded and which modules it affects, with the loose ends flagged.

```sh
Read https://graview.dev/start.md, then turn this repo's decisions into a Graview app.
```

Paste it into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor at the root of your repository. [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md) is the page the agent reads.

## The app, running

This is the declaration below, compiled in your browser by the same compiler `graview check` uses, over the seed below. Press a district; open the problems; take a repair.

*The app the decisions prompt made, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## What the agent declared

**Larkspur decisions**: Larkspur's architecture decision records (docs/adr): each decision, its status and date, what superseded it, and the modules it affects. 2 kinds, 8 acts and 6 rules, each rule with the act that repairs it.

| Kind | Fields | Relations | Records in the seed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `decision` | `number`, `title`, `status`, `date`, `file`, `wholeRepository` | `supersededBy` to `decision`; `affects` to `module` | 14 |
| `module` | `path`, `packageName`, `description` | none | 16 |

### The rules

- **A superseded decision names what superseded it.** Over each decision, when `status == 'superseded'`: requires `present(supersededBy)`. Repaired by “Name what superseded it” (`mark-superseded`).
- **A decision something supersedes says so.** Over each decision, when `present(supersededBy)`: requires `status == 'superseded'`. Repaired by “Mark it superseded” (`mark-superseded`) or “It is not superseded” (`unmark-superseded`).
- **What supersedes a decision is accepted.** Over each decision, when `present(supersededBy)`: requires `supersededBy.status == 'accepted'`. Repaired by “It is not superseded” (`unmark-superseded`).
- **A decision is superseded only by a later one.** Over each decision, when `present(supersededBy)`: requires `supersededBy.date >= date`. Repaired by “It is not superseded” (`unmark-superseded`).
- **A proposal is decided within 90 days.** Over each decision, when `status == 'proposed'`: requires `days(date, today()) <= 90`. Repaired by “Accept it” (`accept-decision`) or “Reject it” (`reject-decision`).
- **An accepted decision affects something.** Over each decision, when `status == 'accepted'`: requires `wholeRepository == true or exists(out('affects'))`. Repaired by “Name a module it affects” (`affect-module`).

## What graview check says

Run on every push, against the committed file:

```sh
npx graview check --document app.json
· rules.proposal-not-left-open: Rule "proposal-not-left-open" reads the clock (today(), now(), a computed field that does, or a kind whose records retire on a date), so the day turning breaks or mends it with nothing changed. A store judges it again only when its host ticks it. — Host it with @graview/ship (openStore, serve and openRemote tick at each midnight, UTC), or call store.tick(now) when the day turns — once a day from a host's own alarm — and its subscribers hear what appeared and cleared.
```

A line starting with a dot is a note, not a warning: advice the checker leaves for a person to weigh.

## How it was made

An agent was given the prompt above and nothing else, at the root of Larkspur: a booking service for small clinics that does not exist, written as a TypeScript monorepo the size of a real one, with sixteen modules, guides and runbooks with gaps, a CODEOWNERS that misses some, fourteen decision records and pinned dependencies. It followed [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md), scaffolded, declared, ran `graview check` until it was clean, opened `graview preview` and reported back. The two files it wrote are committed as they came out of that run.

CI does not run an agent. On every push it checks the committed declaration with `graview check --document`, loads the seed into a store, and opens this page in a browser to see the app mount. To run the prompt again yourself:

```sh
node scripts/fixtures/recipes/larkspur.mjs larkspur
cd larkspur && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm larkspur
# then paste the prompt into your agent
```

The files: [`app.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/decisions/app.json) and [`seed.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/decisions/seed.json) (30 records and 28 relations).

## The declaration, in full

```json
{
  "format": "graview-document",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "name": "Larkspur decisions",
  "description": "Larkspur's architecture decision records (docs/adr): each decision, its status and date, what superseded it, and the modules it affects.",
  "kinds": {
    "decision": {
      "noun": "decision",
      "plural": "decisions",
      "label": "ADR {number}: {title}",
      "description": "One numbered record in docs/adr. Never edited after it is accepted; a changed mind is a new record that supersedes the old one.",
      "fields": {
        "number": { "type": "integer", "required": true, "min": 1, "description": "The record's number, from its file name and heading." },
        "title": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The record's heading, without its number." },
        "status": { "type": "enum", "options": ["proposed", "accepted", "rejected", "superseded"], "required": true, "description": "The record's Status line." },
        "date": { "type": "date", "required": true, "description": "The record's Date line." },
        "file": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Where the record lives in the repository." },
        "wholeRepository": { "type": "boolean", "label": "Affects the whole repository", "description": "The record's Affects line says the whole repository rather than naming modules." }
      },
      "edges": {
        "supersededBy": { "to": ["decision"], "cardinality": "one", "description": "the decision that superseded it", "inverse": "the decisions it supersedes" },
        "affects": { "to": ["module"], "cardinality": "many", "description": "the modules it affects", "inverse": "the decisions that affect it" }
      },
      "fieldRoles": { "when": "date" },
      "glance": ["status", "date", "wholeRepository"]
    },
    "module": {
      "noun": "module",
      "plural": "modules",
      "label": "{path}",
      "description": "A workspace package that pnpm-workspace.yaml takes in: a directory under services/, packages/ or tools/ with its own package.json.",
      "fields": {
        "path": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The directory, from the repository root." },
        "packageName": { "type": "string", "required": true, "label": "Package", "description": "The name in its package.json." },
        "description": { "type": "string", "description": "The description in its package.json." }
      }
    }
  },
  "acts": {
    "add-decision": { "creates": "decision", "title": "Record a decision", "description": "Add a decision record from docs/adr." },
    "add-module": { "creates": "module", "title": "Add a module", "description": "Record a workspace package." },
    "affect-module": { "on": "decision", "connects": "affects", "title": "Say it affects a module", "description": "Name a module this decision affects.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Name a decision that affects it" },
    "unaffect-module": { "on": "decision", "severs": "affects", "title": "Say it no longer affects a module", "description": "Take a module off this decision's Affects line.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a decision off it" },
    "mark-superseded": { "on": "decision", "connects": "supersededBy", "sets": { "status": "superseded" }, "title": "Name what superseded it", "description": "Name the decision that superseded this one, and mark it superseded.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Name a decision it supersedes" },
    "unmark-superseded": { "on": "decision", "severs": "supersededBy", "sets": { "status": "accepted" }, "title": "It is not superseded", "description": "Take back what superseded this decision, and mark it accepted again.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take back a decision it supersedes" },
    "accept-decision": { "on": "decision", "sets": { "status": "accepted" }, "title": "Accept it", "description": "Mark the decision accepted." },
    "reject-decision": { "on": "decision", "sets": { "status": "rejected" }, "title": "Reject it", "description": "Mark the decision rejected: it was considered and not taken." }
  },
  "rules": {
    "superseded-names-successor": {
      "title": "A superseded decision names what superseded it",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "status == 'superseded'",
      "require": "present(supersededBy)",
      "says": "ADR {number} is superseded but does not say by what",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "mark-superseded", "label": "Name what superseded it" }]
    },
    "successor-is-marked-superseded": {
      "title": "A decision something supersedes says so",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "present(supersededBy)",
      "require": "status == 'superseded'",
      "says": "ADR {number} has a successor but its status is {status}",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "mark-superseded", "label": "Mark it superseded" }, { "act": "unmark-superseded", "label": "It is not superseded" }]
    },
    "successor-is-accepted": {
      "title": "What supersedes a decision is accepted",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "present(supersededBy)",
      "require": "supersededBy.status == 'accepted'",
      "says": "ADR {number} is superseded by a decision that is not accepted",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "unmark-superseded", "label": "It is not superseded" }]
    },
    "successor-is-newer": {
      "title": "A decision is superseded only by a later one",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "present(supersededBy)",
      "require": "supersededBy.date >= date",
      "says": "ADR {number} is superseded by a decision dated before it",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "unmark-superseded", "label": "It is not superseded" }]
    },
    "proposal-not-left-open": {
      "title": "A proposal is decided within 90 days",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "status == 'proposed'",
      "require": "days(date, today()) <= 90",
      "says": "ADR {number} has been proposed since {date} and is still open",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "accept-decision", "label": "Accept it" }, { "act": "reject-decision", "label": "Reject it" }]
    },
    "accepted-affects-something": {
      "title": "An accepted decision affects something",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "status == 'accepted'",
      "require": "wholeRepository == true or exists(out('affects'))",
      "says": "ADR {number} is accepted but names no module it affects",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "affect-module", "label": "Name a module it affects" }]
    }
  }
}
```

# Your dependencies, as an upgrade plan

This recipe is what an agent made of one prompt, in a repository it had never seen. Every third-party package, the version pinned against the latest on npm, the modules that use it and the upgrade it needs, with the risky ones flagged.

```sh
Read https://graview.dev/start.md, then turn this repo's dependencies into a Graview app.
```

Paste it into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor at the root of your repository. [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md) is the page the agent reads.

## The app, running

This is the declaration below, compiled in your browser by the same compiler `graview check` uses, over the seed below. Press a district; open the problems; take a repair.

*The app the dependencies prompt made, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## What the agent declared

**Dependencies**: Larkspur's third-party packages: the version each package.json pins, the latest on npm, which modules use each, and the upgrade each needs. 5 kinds, 24 acts and 3 rules, each rule with the act that repairs it.

| Kind | Fields | Relations | Records in the seed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `module` | `path`, `name`, `summary` | `ownedBy` to `person` | 17 |
| `person` | `handle` | none | 7 |
| `package` | `name`, `pinned`, `latest`, `upgrade`, `plan` | `assignedTo` to `person` | 35 |
| `dependency` | `name`, `version`, `section`, `manifest` | `declaredIn` to `module`; `pins` to `package` | 49 |
| `decision` | `number`, `title`, `status`, `date`, `file` | `affects` to `module`; `supersedes` to `decision`; `drops` to `package` | 14 |

### The rules

- **One version per package.** Over each dependency: requires `version == pins.pinned`. Repaired by “Pin it like the others” (`align-pin`).
- **A major upgrade has someone on it.** Over each package, when `upgrade == 'major' && plan != 'drop'`: requires `present(assignedTo)`. Repaired by “Assign its upgrade” (`assign-upgrade`).
- **What an accepted decision drops is planned to go.** Over each package, when `some(in('drops'), status == 'accepted')`: requires `plan == 'drop'`. Repaired by “Plan to drop it” (`plan-drop`).

## What graview check says

Run on every push, against the committed file:

```sh
npx graview check --document app.json
✓ the document compiles and checks clean
```

## How it was made

An agent was given the prompt above and nothing else, at the root of Larkspur: a booking service for small clinics that does not exist, written as a TypeScript monorepo the size of a real one, with sixteen modules, guides and runbooks with gaps, a CODEOWNERS that misses some, fourteen decision records and pinned dependencies. It followed [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md), scaffolded, declared, ran `graview check` until it was clean, opened `graview preview` and reported back. The two files it wrote are committed as they came out of that run.

CI does not run an agent. On every push it checks the committed declaration with `graview check --document`, loads the seed into a store, and opens this page in a browser to see the app mount. To run the prompt again yourself:

```sh
node scripts/fixtures/recipes/larkspur.mjs larkspur
cd larkspur && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm larkspur
# then paste the prompt into your agent
```

The files: [`app.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/dependencies/app.json) and [`seed.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/dependencies/seed.json) (122 records and 142 relations).

## The declaration, in full

```json
{
  "format": "graview-document",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "name": "Dependencies",
  "description": "Larkspur's third-party packages: the version each package.json pins, the latest on npm, which modules use each, and the upgrade each needs.",
  "kinds": {
    "module": {
      "noun": "module",
      "plural": "modules",
      "label": "{path}",
      "description": "A directory with its own package.json: the repository root, a service, a package or a tool.",
      "fields": {
        "path": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "The directory, from the repository root."
        },
        "name": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "The name its package.json gives it."
        },
        "summary": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "The description its package.json gives it."
        }
      },
      "edges": {
        "ownedBy": {
          "to": [
            "person"
          ],
          "cardinality": "many",
          "description": "who CODEOWNERS says reviews it",
          "inverse": "the modules they review"
        }
      }
    },
    "person": {
      "noun": "person",
      "plural": "people",
      "label": "{handle}",
      "description": "Someone .github/CODEOWNERS names.",
      "fields": {
        "handle": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "Their GitHub handle."
        }
      }
    },
    "package": {
      "noun": "package",
      "plural": "packages",
      "label": "{name}",
      "description": "A third-party npm package some package.json depends on.",
      "fields": {
        "name": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "Its name on npm."
        },
        "pinned": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "The version the repository pins (the highest, where modules differ)."
        },
        "latest": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "The latest version on npm (npm view <name> version)."
        },
        "upgrade": {
          "type": "enum",
          "options": [
            "major",
            "minor",
            "patch",
            "none"
          ],
          "required": true,
          "description": "How far pinned is from latest. Major means a breaking change: the first non-zero number of the version moves."
        },
        "plan": {
          "type": "enum",
          "options": [
            "upgrade",
            "hold",
            "drop"
          ],
          "description": "What the team means to do with it."
        }
      },
      "edges": {
        "assignedTo": {
          "to": [
            "person"
          ],
          "cardinality": "one",
          "description": "who is doing its upgrade",
          "inverse": "the upgrades they are doing"
        }
      }
    },
    "dependency": {
      "noun": "dependency",
      "plural": "dependencies",
      "label": "{name}@{version} in {manifest}",
      "description": "One line of one package.json: a module depending on a package at a version.",
      "fields": {
        "name": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "The package name as the line writes it."
        },
        "version": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "The version the line pins."
        },
        "section": {
          "type": "enum",
          "options": [
            "dependencies",
            "devDependencies"
          ],
          "required": true,
          "description": "Which list of the package.json it is in."
        },
        "manifest": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "The package.json it is in."
        }
      },
      "edges": {
        "declaredIn": {
          "to": [
            "module"
          ],
          "cardinality": "one",
          "description": "the module whose package.json has this line",
          "inverse": "its third-party dependencies"
        },
        "pins": {
          "to": [
            "package"
          ],
          "cardinality": "one",
          "description": "the package it pins",
          "inverse": "the modules' lines that pin it"
        }
      }
    },
    "decision": {
      "noun": "decision",
      "plural": "decisions",
      "label": "ADR {number}: {title}",
      "description": "An architecture decision record in docs/adr.",
      "fields": {
        "number": {
          "type": "integer",
          "required": true,
          "min": 1,
          "description": "Its number."
        },
        "title": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "Its heading."
        },
        "status": {
          "type": "enum",
          "options": [
            "proposed",
            "accepted",
            "superseded"
          ],
          "required": true,
          "description": "Its Status line."
        },
        "date": {
          "type": "date",
          "description": "Its Date line."
        },
        "file": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "Its file, from the repository root."
        }
      },
      "edges": {
        "affects": {
          "to": [
            "module"
          ],
          "cardinality": "many",
          "description": "the modules its Affects line names",
          "inverse": "the decisions that affect it"
        },
        "supersedes": {
          "to": [
            "decision"
          ],
          "cardinality": "many",
          "description": "the decisions it replaces",
          "inverse": "the decision that replaced it"
        },
        "drops": {
          "to": [
            "package"
          ],
          "cardinality": "many",
          "description": "the packages it makes unnecessary",
          "inverse": "the decisions that drop it"
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "acts": {
    "add-module": {
      "creates": "module",
      "title": "Add a module",
      "description": "Record a directory with its own package.json."
    },
    "add-person": {
      "creates": "person",
      "title": "Add a person",
      "description": "Record someone who reviews or upgrades code."
    },
    "add-package": {
      "creates": "package",
      "title": "Add a package",
      "description": "Record a third-party package the repository depends on."
    },
    "add-dependency": {
      "creates": "dependency",
      "title": "Add a dependency",
      "description": "Record one line of one package.json."
    },
    "add-decision": {
      "creates": "decision",
      "title": "Add a decision",
      "description": "Record an architecture decision record."
    },
    "give-owner": {
      "on": "module",
      "connects": "ownedBy",
      "title": "Give it an owner",
      "description": "Say who reviews this module.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Give them a module"
    },
    "take-owner": {
      "on": "module",
      "severs": "ownedBy",
      "title": "Take an owner off",
      "description": "Say this person no longer reviews this module.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a module off them"
    },
    "assign-upgrade": {
      "on": "package",
      "connects": "assignedTo",
      "title": "Assign its upgrade",
      "description": "Say who is doing this package's upgrade.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Give them an upgrade"
    },
    "unassign-upgrade": {
      "on": "package",
      "severs": "assignedTo",
      "title": "Unassign its upgrade",
      "description": "Say nobody is doing this package's upgrade now.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take an upgrade off them"
    },
    "plan-drop": {
      "on": "package",
      "sets": {
        "plan": "drop"
      },
      "title": "Plan to drop it",
      "description": "Say the team means to remove this package."
    },
    "plan-upgrade": {
      "on": "package",
      "sets": {
        "plan": "upgrade"
      },
      "title": "Plan to upgrade it",
      "description": "Say the team means to move this package to its latest version."
    },
    "plan-hold": {
      "on": "package",
      "sets": {
        "plan": "hold"
      },
      "title": "Hold it where it is",
      "description": "Say the team means to keep this package at its pinned version."
    },
    "place-in": {
      "on": "dependency",
      "connects": "declaredIn",
      "title": "Say which module has it",
      "description": "Say whose package.json this line is in.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Add a dependency line"
    },
    "take-out-of": {
      "on": "dependency",
      "severs": "declaredIn",
      "title": "Take it out of its module",
      "description": "Say this line is in no module's package.json now.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a dependency line out"
    },
    "pin-package": {
      "on": "dependency",
      "connects": "pins",
      "title": "Say which package it pins",
      "description": "Say which package this line pins.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Add a line that pins it"
    },
    "unpin-package": {
      "on": "dependency",
      "severs": "pins",
      "title": "Unlink its package",
      "description": "Say this line pins no recorded package.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Unlink a line that pins it"
    },
    "align-pin": {
      "on": "dependency",
      "sets": {
        "version": {
          "expr": "pins.pinned"
        }
      },
      "title": "Pin it like the others",
      "description": "Set this line to the version the rest of the repository pins."
    },
    "affect-module": {
      "on": "decision",
      "connects": "affects",
      "title": "Say it affects a module",
      "description": "Add a module to this decision's Affects line.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Name a decision that affects it"
    },
    "unaffect-module": {
      "on": "decision",
      "severs": "affects",
      "title": "Say it no longer affects a module",
      "description": "Take a module off this decision's Affects line.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a decision off it"
    },
    "supersede": {
      "on": "decision",
      "connects": "supersedes",
      "title": "Say what it supersedes",
      "description": "Say which decision this one replaces.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Say what replaced it"
    },
    "unsupersede": {
      "on": "decision",
      "severs": "supersedes",
      "title": "Take back what it supersedes",
      "description": "Say this decision no longer replaces that one.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take back what replaced it"
    },
    "drop-package": {
      "on": "decision",
      "connects": "drops",
      "title": "Say it drops a package",
      "description": "Say this decision makes a package unnecessary.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Name a decision that drops it"
    },
    "keep-package": {
      "on": "decision",
      "severs": "drops",
      "title": "Say it keeps a package",
      "description": "Say this decision does not make that package unnecessary.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a decision that drops it off"
    },
    "accept-decision": {
      "on": "decision",
      "sets": {
        "status": "accepted"
      },
      "title": "Accept it",
      "description": "Mark this decision accepted."
    }
  },
  "rules": {
    "one-version-per-package": {
      "title": "One version per package",
      "over": "dependency",
      "require": "version == pins.pinned",
      "says": "{manifest} pins {name} at {version}; the rest of the repository pins another version",
      "repairs": [
        {
          "act": "align-pin",
          "label": "Pin it like the others"
        }
      ]
    },
    "major-upgrade-has-someone": {
      "title": "A major upgrade has someone on it",
      "over": "package",
      "when": "upgrade == 'major' && plan != 'drop'",
      "require": "present(assignedTo)",
      "says": "{name} is pinned at {pinned} and {latest} is out: a major upgrade nobody is assigned",
      "repairs": [
        {
          "act": "assign-upgrade",
          "label": "Assign its upgrade"
        }
      ]
    },
    "dropped-by-a-decision": {
      "title": "What an accepted decision drops is planned to go",
      "over": "package",
      "when": "some(in('drops'), status == 'accepted')",
      "require": "plan == 'drop'",
      "says": "An accepted decision drops {name}, and it is not planned to go",
      "repairs": [
        {
          "act": "plan-drop",
          "label": "Plan to drop it"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "brand": {
    "accents": {
      "decision": 175
    }
  }
}
```

---

A Graview recipe: Every third-party package, the version pinned against the latest on npm, the modules that use it and the upgrade it needs, with the risky ones flagged.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/dependencies.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/docs.html

# Your docs, as an app

This recipe is what an agent made of one prompt, in a repository it had never seen. The repository's docs, the modules they cover and who owns each, with every module that has no doc or no owner flagged and the repair offered.

```sh
Read https://graview.dev/start.md, then turn this repo's docs into a Graview app.
```

Paste it into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor at the root of your repository. [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md) is the page the agent reads.

## The app, running

This is the declaration below, compiled in your browser by the same compiler `graview check` uses, over the seed below. Press a district; open the problems; take a repair.

*The app the docs prompt made, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## What the agent declared

**Larkspur docs**: Larkspur's docs, the modules they cover, who owns each module, and where the docs and the owners run out. 4 kinds, 18 acts and 5 rules, each rule with the act that repairs it.

| Kind | Fields | Relations | Records in the seed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `module` | `path`, `packageName`, `summary`, `area`, `readme` | `ownedBy` to `person`; `documentedIn` to `doc` | 16 |
| `doc` | `title`, `path`, `section`, `lastReviewed` | `ownedBy` to `person` | 17 |
| `decision` | `number`, `title`, `path`, `status`, `decided`, `wholeRepository` | `affects` to `module`; `supersedes` to `decision` | 14 |
| `person` | `handle` | none | 7 |

### The rules

- **Every module has a doc.** Over each module: requires `exists(out('documentedIn'))`. Repaired by “Point it at a doc” (`document-in`).
- **Every module has an owner.** Over each module: requires `exists(out('ownedBy'))`. Repaired by “Give it an owner” (`give-module-owner`).
- **Every module has a README.** Over each module: requires `present(readme)`. Repaired by “Record its README” (`edit-module`).
- **Every guide, runbook and API doc covers a module.** Over each doc, when `section == 'guide' or section == 'runbook' or section == 'api'`: requires `exists(in('documentedIn'))`. Repaired by “Say which module it covers” (`cover-module`).
- **A superseded decision names its successor.** Over each decision, when `status == 'superseded'`: requires `exists(in('supersedes'))`. Repaired by “Say which record supersedes it” (`supersede`).

## What graview check says

Run on every push, against the committed file:

```sh
npx graview check --document app.json
✓ the document compiles and checks clean
```

## How it was made

An agent was given the prompt above and nothing else, at the root of Larkspur: a booking service for small clinics that does not exist, written as a TypeScript monorepo the size of a real one, with sixteen modules, guides and runbooks with gaps, a CODEOWNERS that misses some, fourteen decision records and pinned dependencies. It followed [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md), scaffolded, declared, ran `graview check` until it was clean, opened `graview preview` and reported back. The two files it wrote are committed as they came out of that run.

CI does not run an agent. On every push it checks the committed declaration with `graview check --document`, loads the seed into a store, and opens this page in a browser to see the app mount. To run the prompt again yourself:

```sh
node scripts/fixtures/recipes/larkspur.mjs larkspur
cd larkspur && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm larkspur
# then paste the prompt into your agent
```

The files: [`app.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/docs/app.json) and [`seed.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/docs/seed.json) (54 records and 78 relations).

## The declaration, in full

```json
{
  "format": "graview-document",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "name": "Larkspur docs",
  "description": "Larkspur's docs, the modules they cover, who owns each module, and where the docs and the owners run out.",
  "kinds": {
    "module": {
      "noun": "module",
      "plural": "modules",
      "label": "{path}",
      "description": "A workspace directory with its own package.json, under services/, packages/ or tools/.",
      "fields": {
        "path": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The directory, from the repository root." },
        "packageName": { "type": "string", "label": "Package", "description": "The name in its package.json." },
        "summary": { "type": "string", "description": "The description in its package.json." },
        "area": { "type": "enum", "options": ["service", "package", "tool"], "required": true, "description": "Which workspace folder it sits in." },
        "readme": { "type": "string", "label": "README", "description": "Its own README.md, if it has one." }
      },
      "edges": {
        "ownedBy": { "to": ["person"], "cardinality": "many", "description": "who CODEOWNERS says reviews it", "inverse": "the modules they own" },
        "documentedIn": { "to": ["doc"], "cardinality": "many", "description": "the docs that cover it", "inverse": "the modules it covers" }
      }
    },
    "doc": {
      "noun": "doc",
      "plural": "docs",
      "label": "{title}",
      "description": "A Markdown file under docs/ (outside the decision records) or the repository's README.",
      "fields": {
        "title": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Its first heading." },
        "path": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The file, from the repository root." },
        "section": { "type": "enum", "options": ["overview", "guide", "runbook", "api", "index"], "required": true, "description": "Where it sits in docs/." },
        "lastReviewed": { "type": "date", "label": "Last reviewed", "description": "The date on its Last reviewed line." }
      },
      "edges": {
        "ownedBy": { "to": ["person"], "cardinality": "many", "description": "who CODEOWNERS says reviews it", "inverse": "the docs they own" }
      },
      "fieldRoles": { "when": "lastReviewed" }
    },
    "decision": {
      "noun": "decision record",
      "plural": "decision records",
      "label": "ADR {number}: {title}",
      "description": "A numbered decision record under docs/adr/.",
      "fields": {
        "number": { "type": "integer", "required": true, "min": 1, "description": "Its number." },
        "title": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Its heading, without the number." },
        "path": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The file, from the repository root." },
        "status": { "type": "enum", "options": ["proposed", "accepted", "superseded"], "required": true, "description": "Its Status line." },
        "decided": { "type": "date", "label": "Date", "description": "Its Date line." },
        "wholeRepository": { "type": "boolean", "label": "Affects the whole repository", "description": "Its Affects line names the whole repository rather than modules." }
      },
      "edges": {
        "affects": { "to": ["module"], "cardinality": "many", "description": "the modules its Affects line names", "inverse": "the decisions that affect it" },
        "supersedes": { "to": ["decision"], "cardinality": "one", "description": "the earlier decision it replaces", "inverse": "the decision that replaced it" }
      },
      "fieldRoles": { "when": "decided" },
      "glance": ["number", "status", "decided"]
    },
    "person": {
      "noun": "person",
      "plural": "people",
      "label": "{handle}",
      "description": "Someone .github/CODEOWNERS names.",
      "fields": {
        "handle": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Their handle in CODEOWNERS." }
      }
    }
  },
  "acts": {
    "add-module": { "creates": "module", "title": "Add a module", "description": "Record a workspace directory with its own package.json." },
    "add-doc": { "creates": "doc", "title": "Add a doc", "description": "Record a Markdown file under docs/." },
    "add-decision": { "creates": "decision", "title": "Add a decision record", "description": "Record a numbered decision under docs/adr/." },
    "add-person": { "creates": "person", "title": "Add a person", "description": "Record someone CODEOWNERS names." },

    "give-module-owner": { "on": "module", "connects": "ownedBy", "title": "Give the module an owner", "description": "Say who reviews this module.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Give them a module" },
    "take-module-owner": { "on": "module", "severs": "ownedBy", "title": "Take an owner off the module", "description": "Say this person no longer reviews this module.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a module off them" },
    "give-doc-owner": { "on": "doc", "connects": "ownedBy", "title": "Give the doc an owner", "description": "Say who reviews this doc.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Give them a doc" },
    "take-doc-owner": { "on": "doc", "severs": "ownedBy", "title": "Take an owner off the doc", "description": "Say this person no longer reviews this doc.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a doc off them" },

    "document-in": { "on": "module", "connects": "documentedIn", "title": "Point it at a doc", "description": "Say which doc covers this module.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Say it covers a module" },
    "cover-module": { "on": "doc", "connects": "documentedIn", "title": "Say which module it covers", "description": "Name a module this doc covers.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Point it at this doc" },
    "undocument-in": { "on": "module", "severs": "documentedIn", "title": "Take a doc off it", "description": "Say this doc no longer covers this module.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Say it no longer covers a module" },

    "add-affected": { "on": "decision", "connects": "affects", "title": "Name a module it affects", "description": "Add a module to its Affects line.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Name a decision that affects it" },
    "remove-affected": { "on": "decision", "severs": "affects", "title": "Take a module off it", "description": "Take a module off its Affects line.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a decision off it" },
    "supersede": { "on": "decision", "connects": "supersedes", "title": "Say what it supersedes", "description": "Name the earlier decision this one replaces.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Say what superseded it" },
    "unsupersede": { "on": "decision", "severs": "supersedes", "title": "Take back what it supersedes", "description": "Say this decision no longer replaces that one.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take back what superseded it" },

    "accept-decision": { "on": "decision", "sets": { "status": "accepted" }, "title": "Accept it", "description": "Mark the decision accepted." },
    "propose-decision": { "on": "decision", "sets": { "status": "proposed" }, "title": "Put it back to proposed", "description": "Mark the decision proposed again." },
    "mark-superseded": { "on": "decision", "sets": { "status": "superseded" }, "title": "Mark it superseded", "description": "Mark the decision superseded by a later one." }
  },
  "rules": {
    "module-has-doc": {
      "title": "Every module has a doc",
      "over": "module",
      "require": "exists(out('documentedIn'))",
      "says": "No doc covers {path}",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "document-in", "label": "Point it at a doc" }]
    },
    "module-has-owner": {
      "title": "Every module has an owner",
      "over": "module",
      "require": "exists(out('ownedBy'))",
      "says": "{path} has no owner in CODEOWNERS",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "give-module-owner", "label": "Give it an owner" }]
    },
    "module-has-readme": {
      "title": "Every module has a README",
      "over": "module",
      "require": "present(readme)",
      "says": "{path} has no README.md",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "edit-module", "label": "Record its README" }]
    },
    "doc-covers-a-module": {
      "title": "Every guide, runbook and API doc covers a module",
      "over": "doc",
      "when": "section == 'guide' or section == 'runbook' or section == 'api'",
      "require": "exists(in('documentedIn'))",
      "says": "{title} ({path}) names no module it covers",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "cover-module", "label": "Say which module it covers" }]
    },
    "superseded-has-successor": {
      "title": "A superseded decision names its successor",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "status == 'superseded'",
      "require": "exists(in('supersedes'))",
      "says": "{title} is marked superseded but no record supersedes it",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "supersede", "label": "Say which record supersedes it" }]
    }
  }
}
```

# Live demos

These are live demos of Graview: the example garden, running in this page. Nothing here is a screenshot. Each frame is the example garden, mounted on this page by `@graview/embed` from the same declaration, at a different place in it. [The garden, grown](https://graview.dev/progression.html) has all sixteen chapters, each with what the declaration gained.

## The city, at altitude

Every kind is a district; every record a building on its own plot; every edge a road with its words on it. Drag the ground, press a district, come down to a plot.

*The example garden at altitude, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## The routed face

The same store as ordinary pages — here in the garden's own design: an almanac over the same acts, rules and log.

*The garden's routed pages, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## The studio

The declaration itself, open as a graph, edited with ordinary acts and checked before the change lands.

*The declaration open in the studio, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## A seat for an agent

The same acts a person has, narrowed by the same policy, attributed in the same log.

*The garden with an agent's seat, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## The example apps

Each was built to prove a claim the others could not, and each is opened in a real browser on every push. They live under `apps/` in the repository; `pnpm apps` opens the desk, which opens the rest.

- [discography](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/tree/main/apps/discography): The example at real size: Tech N9ne's discography from MusicBrainz — 1,177 songs, 568 artists, 479 releases.
- [gauntlet](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/tree/main/apps/gauntlet): The example built to be awkward: ten years of a conference's program, with every shape of data the walks found by accident declared on purpose.
- [rota](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/tree/main/apps/rota): The product-grade example: a volunteer shift roster, branded, permissioned, remembered, embedded and open in its own studio.
- [seedbed](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/tree/main/apps/seedbed): A community garden, and the chapters the docs teach from. It opens on the example garden; Start empty gives the blank graph, where onboarding is filling it in.
- [todo](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/tree/main/apps/todo): The example. A todo list, because nobody has to be taught what one is.

# This site is a Graview app

graview.dev is a Graview app: one declaration, [`apps/site/app.json`](https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/graview/blob/main/apps/site/app.json), and 375 records written out of the repository by `node scripts/site-docs.mjs`. Every page the site serves is one of those records, rendered as static HTML by `renderPlace` from `@graview/pages/static` in the site's own design, so a search engine and a model read plain pages, and none of them can say what the records do not.

## The site, running

This is that declaration, compiled in your browser by the same compiler `graview check` uses, over the same records the pages are rendered from: the city of its packages, skills, check findings and pages. Press a district; come down to a record; switch to its pages.

*graview.dev as a Graview app, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## What it declares

**graview.dev**: Graview's own site and docs as a Graview app: every page graview.dev serves is a record, written out of the repository by scripts/site-docs.mjs and rendered by renderPlace, beside the packages, skills, checks and recipes it is about. 13 kinds, each read out of the tree:

| Kind | What it is | Records |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | An address graview.dev serves: a web page, the Markdown twin beside it, or a file for crawlers and models. | 58 |
| `package` | An npm package Graview ships, read off its package.json, its README.md and its barrel. | 14 |
| `entry` | One subpath a package exports, as a product imports it. | 92 |
| `skill` | An authoring skill an assistant reads before it changes a Graview app, read off its SKILL.md. | 19 |
| `check` | A thing graview check can say, read out of the checker's source. | 105 |
| `command` | A graview subcommand, read off the help the CLI prints. | 13 |
| `concept` | One of the ideas a Graview declaration is made of: not in the repository, the reason it is shaped the way it is. | 7 |
| `recipe` | The prompt on the front page with a different task, and the declaration and seed an agent made of it, under docs/site/recipes/. | 3 |
| `chapter` | A step of the garden, grown: a declaration that passes its own check, opened in a browser on every push. | 16 |
| `example` | An example app in the repository, described by its own package.json. | 5 |
| `question` | A question the front page answers plainly, read off its FAQ. | 7 |
| `release` | A version every package shares, as the releases page says it: when npm published it, what came in it in a few plain lines, and what a host must know before upgrading. Written by hand with the Version packages pull request (apps/site/releases.json). | 35 |
| `scaffold` | What graview create writes, read from the generator itself. | 1 |

## How a page is made

`scripts/site-docs.mjs` reads the repository — each package's `package.json`, `README.md` and barrel, each skill's `SKILL.md`, the checker's source, the CLI's help, the recipes, the chapters — and writes a record for each, then a page record for every address graview.dev serves, related to what it is about. Each page record is rendered by `renderPlace` with the site's design, `apps/site/design.mjs`: a docs page in the docs shell, the front page, the tour and the long version filled into their hand-designed pages (`apps/site/pages/`), and `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, the sitemap and `start.md` as records too. `tests/site.test.ts` holds every served address to a record, and the declaration to `graview check`.

```sh
npx graview check --document apps/site/app.json
node scripts/site-docs.mjs --check
```

---

graview.dev is itself a Graview app: one declaration and the records written out of the repository, every page rendered from a record by renderPlace, and the whole of it live on this page.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/site.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt
